claim: `deflate_part` can accept a non-last PNG part whose last bytes are still inside miniz_oxide's internal buffer. Those bytes are lost, so the IDAT stream breaks. The px.js output cap (`n + ceil(n/65535)*5 + 64`, px.js:716) assumes stored blocks of 64 KB. At level 2 (PNG_LEVEL), incompressible input is written as stored blocks of about 31 KB, which needs about twice that overhead.
scenario: Checked against miniz_oxide 0.8.9 `compress_inner` / `flush_output_buffer` (core.rs:2237-2324, 2160-2178). A tile layer or export whose filtered RGBA bytes are close to uniform noise in all four channels, for example an imported RGBA noise texture with random alpha, at least ~720 px wide. At 15,000 px wide a part is 139 rows = 8,340,139 bytes. miniz flushes a 'fat' block every 31,745 literals (`buf_fat`, core.rs:1929). Each block is expanded, so it is written stored with 5 bytes of overhead: 263 x 5 + 5 for the sync marker = 1,320 bytes, against the 704 the cap allows. The cap therefore runs out only in the final `TDEFLFlush::Sync` flush_block. About 616 bytes go to `local_buf` (`flush_remaining > 0`), and compress returns `(Okay, len, cap)`. `deflate_part` checks only `status == Okay && consumed == len`, so it returns `cap` as success. The part has no tail and no sync marker, so every non-last IDAT part is cut short. Only the last part (Finish, which needs Done) retries. The same writer encodes layer uploads (inpaint_upload.js:49 `encodeTilePixels` -> inpaint_encode.js:89 `writePng`), so the layer PNG in the mirror is also corrupt, and with it the .scumble document and autosave. The layer is lost on reopen. tools/px_test.js:3095-3100 tests noise only as a small, last (Finish) part at level 1.
fix: In crates/px/src/png.rs `deflate_part`, also return -1 when `written == out.len()`. Pending output in miniz can only exist when the buffer is full. The caller already retries with a doubled cap, and an exact fit only costs one harmless retry. Optionally size the first cap for 31 KB stored blocks in px.js `pngPart` and `zlib`, `n + Math.ceil(n / 31744) * 5 + 64`, so noise does not compress twice. Add a px_test case: a non-last level-2 part of 4096x256 crypto-random RGBA, followed by a last part, inflated together. Today's pngPartCases (w=700, at most 64 rows, 60 % flat alpha) and the noise case (900x40, last, level 1) cannot reach this. After the .rs edit, rebuild both builds with tools/build_px.py, then run --check.
why: Confirmed from the code and by running the snapshot's own px.wasm and px_scalar.wasm in Node. Nothing was built and the repo was not touched; the scripts are in the scratchpad's verify_deflate folder. In miniz_oxide 0.8.9, compress_inner (core.rs:2237-2324) runs the final Sync flush_block once all input has been consumed. When fewer than OUT_BUF_SIZE bytes of output space are left, the block goes to local_buf. CallbackBuf::flush_output (core.rs:470-490) copies only what fits and keeps the rest in flush_remaining. flush_output_buffer then returns (Okay, src.len(), out.len()), because finished is false on a Sync flush. deflate_part (png.rs:18-27) checks only `status == Okay && consumed == len`, so it returns `cap` as success. The tail of the last block and the sync marker are lost. A mid-stream overflow is caught: compress_normal returns early with src_pos < len, so the call returns -1. The last part is also safe, because Finish needs Done. Measured: a non-last level-2 part of random RGBA at 15000x139, 720x256, 700x256 and 4096x256 comes back exactly `cap` bytes long with both wasm builds. Inflated with a following part, it fails with 'unexpected end of file' or 'invalid stored block lengths'. The cause is the one claimed: incompressible data is stored in blocks of about 31 KB (buf_fat at core.rs:1929), which costs 5 bytes per 31,745, while px.js:716 allows 5 per 65,535 plus 64. The same writer is used for layer uploads into the mirror and the .scumble (inpaint_upload.js:49 -> inpaint_encode.js encodeTilePixels -> PngStreamWriter) and for exports (encodeRows). Nothing decodes the file after writing, so the corrupt PNG is stored silently. The trigger is narrow. Uniform RGB with alpha 255 (ratio 0.86), uniform RGB with alpha 200-255 (0.994) and Gaussian sigma 60 on all four channels (1.0000, under the cap) all inflate fine. Only near-uniform high-entropy bytes in all four channels, across a part of about 0.72 MB or more, break, for example an imported RGBA white-noise texture. It stays at must because, when it hits, the saved document and autosave lose the layer without any warning, and the fix is one line.

claim: Settings > Local files > Clean up (files.prune) keeps only the files named in four places: the open documents' current state (getValue: the current layers, the base, the last 100 history entries), the closed tabs, plugin and extra data (referencedFileKeys, host.js:5875-5897, used at shell.js:2495), and the earlier autosave generations (main.js:1118). The undo and redo stacks and the named snapshots are not scanned. A 'layers' undo step (delete, add, reorder or group a layer) puts the layer back with its old ref and dirty flag as they were (applySnapshot, inpaint_canvas.js:14551), so a layer that was clean is never uploaded again. A 'canvas' undo puts back `snap.base` with its old ref and does not upload it again (14661). setValue then drops a pixel layer whose file is missing with only a console.warn (24899-24901): `failed` counts filter layers only, so no leftOut note is shown.
scenario: The session has been open for some hours. The user made a layer more than an hour ago, so prune's one-hour rule does not protect its file, and autosave generation 1 (the state at this session's start) does not name it. The user deletes the layer (or flattens, or merges into the base), runs Clean up, and the dialog's 'no open document references' removes the layer's PNG (or the old base). Then the user presses Ctrl+Z. The picture looks right, because the pixels are in memory, but the layer's ref (or the base's) names the deleted file and nothing re-uploads it. The 15 s autosave writes that name. At the next start, with no copy on ComfyUI (offline, --no-comfy, or an API-only user, who has no copy anywhere), the base gives 'Could not restore canvas' and the whole document is gone, or the layer silently disappears. Ctrl+S refuses with '<file> is not in the local store; the document was not saved' (documents.js:193), and a run fails with 'neither on the server nor in the local store'.
fix: Walk ed.undo, ed.redo and ed.snapshots[].snap in referencedFileKeys and add every ref they hold to the keep set: snap.base.ref, the ref and maskRef of each layer in layers / canvas / turn snapshots, and the selection, LUT and plate refs (filter steps too). As a backstop, mark a restored layer (and a restored canvas-step base) for re-upload in applySnapshot when its mirror file is gone. Count a pixel layer that fails to load in setValue's `failed`, so the leftOut note names it.
why: Found from two slices. documents verifier (kept must): Clean up keeps the union of host.referencedFileKeys (host.js:5875-5895), autosave.referencedKeys (generations 1, 2 and the crash copies, autosave.js:150-173) and documents.keepKeys (jobs in flight only). referencedFileKeys walks getValue(), base.ref, pluginData, docExtra and the closed tabs. It never walks ed.undo or ed.redo. The 'layers' branch of applySnapshot (inpaint_canvas.js:14547-14559) restores {...l} from snapshotLayer, a shallow copy that keeps ref and dirty. The 'canvas' branch (14657-14666) puts snap.base back with its old ref, and nothing re-uploads a base. So if Clean up runs after a delete or a crop older than prune's one-hour mtime rule, an undo leaves the layer or the base naming a deleted mirror file; the autosave names that file, so the layer (or the whole picture) is gone at the next start. Ctrl+S fails at documents.js:192 unless fetchMissing can get the file from a server that still has it, which API-only users do not have. canvas-c verifier (lowered to should): the code matches; the files:prune handler (main.js:1113-1120) adds only the earlier sessions' autosave generations, not the current session; named snapshots are never walked; setValue drops a pixel layer that fails to load with only a console.warn (`failed` is counted only in the filter branch, 24846, 24903-24904). It lowered the severity because the path needs an explicit cleanup click, an undo across it, and no copy on the server: with ComfyUI connected, handleView (files.js:178-186) fetches the forwarded copy back, and a .scumble save fails loudly rather than silently. This report keeps must: both verifiers confirmed the path, the loss is silent until the next start, and an API-only user has no copy anywhere. The walk alone is small; the backstop and the setValue note make it medium.

claim: fal, Replicate and WaveSpeed give up a job that is already submitted and paid for the first time a status read fails: a dropped connection, a 429 or a 5xx ends the run. Each also fetches the finished picture exactly once. The places: fal.js:254-255 (status), 260-261 (result JSON), 321/335/346 (image); replicate.js:206-207 and 213; wavespeed.js:298-299 and 307. The result downloads of Comfy Router and the Partner API are single tries as well (comfyrouter.js:879 through util.fetchImage; comfypartner.js:188). In the same folder, BFL (bfl.js:129-150, its comment: "the job is submitted and paid for"), ToAPIs (LOST_QUERIES, DOWNLOAD_TRIES), Magnific (POLL_FAILURES_MAX, DOWNLOAD_TRIES), Oxen and Comfy Cloud all ride out up to 5 failed reads and retry the download. The rule has drifted between adapters. None of the three error texts names the request id, so the user cannot find the picture in the provider's dashboard either.
scenario: A Topaz upscale on fal of a large crop (UPSCALE_WAIT_MS, 30 min), or a GPT Image 2.6 edit on WaveSpeed. A few minutes in, the Wi-Fi drops for a second, or fal's status route answers one 502. ctx.fetch throws "fetch failed" (or !r.ok) and queued() throws. The status line says "fal.ai status: Bad Gateway". The job finishes on fal and is billed, and its picture is never fetched. The same happens when the CDN download of a finished picture fails once, or when BFL's short-lived sample URL behind the Router (comfyrouter.js BFL dialect) times out once.
fix: Add one shared polled-job helper in util.js modelled on bfl.js. It retries up to 5 failed status reads in a row (a thrown fetch, 429, 5xx, or a body that is not JSON; Retry-After respected) on ctx.sleep. It tries the result JSON and the image download 3 times. The final error names the request id and says the job may still finish and be charged. Use it in fal.queued, replicate edit, wavespeed edit, comfyrouter download and comfypartner. Add one fake-fetch test per adapter: a 502 in the middle of the poll still lands the picture.
why: Confirmed in the snapshot. fal.js queued() at 254-255 throws on the first !r.ok status read, and a network error from ctx.fetch goes up uncaught. The result JSON (260-261) and the picture (321/335/346 through util.fetchImage, which tries once, util.js:20-21) are fetched once each. replicate.js:206-207 and 213 do the same, and wavespeed.js:298-299 and 307 too. comfyrouter.js download() (875-880) and comfypartner.js:188 fetch the picture once. contextFor's ctx.fetch (index.js:485-488) only adds the abort signal and never retries. bfl.js:129-158 shows the intended rule (5 misses with backoff, 3 download tries). Neither verified.json nor BUGS.md Open lists this. On a 30-minute fal Topaz upscale, polled about every 1.5 s, one 502 or a second of Wi-Fi loss ends a paid job, and the job's picture is never fetched. None of the error texts names the request id.

claim: Uploads that keep the picture's own file name get a free name from the local mirror only (files.js:87). These are a loaded or pasted base (inpaint_canvas.js:18534), dropped image and reference layers (16965) and plates (15487), all through uploadBlob(..., {overwrite:false}). The upload is forwarded to ComfyUI with overwrite=true (files.js:143). Before a local run, ensureOnServer checks the server by name only: the in-memory `known` set, then HEAD /view (files.js:194-207). So a same-named file of another client, or one left from an older session, is taken to be this picture.
scenario: The installed app and the portable copy, or two PCs, use one ComfyUI (local or a RunPod pod). The Inpaint Canvas node in the browser on that server counts as a client too. Copy A pastes picture P1. Chromium names it image.png, A's mirror stores input/inpaint_canvas/image.png, and A runs once. Copy B pastes P2. Its own mirror also picks image.png and pushes it with overwrite=true, which replaces P1 on the server. If the browser node had pasted an image.png, its file is replaced too, so its saved workflow now opens P2. A's next local run on a tab with no visible layers sends base = this.base.ref, i.e. image.png (inpaint_canvas.js:25026-25032). Untouched references go by their own ref too (25066). `known` says the file is there, nothing is uploaded, and the canvas node crops P2: the result layer lands with another picture's content. Single-copy variant: after Settings > Local files > Clean up (or with a fresh profile), a picture loaded while ComfyUI is offline reuses a name the server still holds for an old picture. HEAD answers 200 and the run uses the old picture.
fix: Give the overwrite:false uploads content-addressed names (stem_<hash8>.ext, hashed from the bytes in handleUpload/handleRawUpload or in the editor's callers), so that one name means the same bytes in the mirror and on the server. Until then, at least compare the server's Content-Length from HEAD with the mirror file's size in ensureOnServer and re-upload on a mismatch, and never forward a name that is not a hash with overwrite=true.
why: The code matches the claim. loadFile (inpaint_canvas.js:18533-18534) and the image-layer and plate drops (16965, 15487) call uploadBlob(file, stem+ext, {overwrite:false}), so the base keeps its original name: a pasted picture is 'image.png'. files.js:87 picks a name that is only free in the local mirror. pushToServer then forwards it with overwrite=true (files.js:143, 153). ensureOnServer (files.js:194-207) checks the server by name only: first the in-memory known set, then HEAD /view returning 200. serializeForPrompt (inpaint_canvas.js:25026-25031) sends this.base.ref when no visible non-control layer exists, and untouched references go by l.ref (25066). Two concrete cases. (1) The ComfyUI node in the browser builds the same editor code with the same SUBFOLDER 'inpaint_canvas', and its uploads use ComfyUI's own server-side collision rule. Scumble's mirror sequence is independent, so its overwrite=true push replaces the node's same-named file on the server, and the node's saved workflow then loads the wrong picture. (2) A picture loaded while ComfyUI is offline (after Clean up, a fresh profile or the portable copy) reuses a name the server still holds. HEAD returns 200 and the local run crops the old picture. Neither docs/BUGS.md nor verified.json lists this. HISTORY.md:5334 calls the free-name rule 'harmless'. Only local runs on a bare base or on untouched references are affected; API runs crop from the editor's own pixels.

claim: The first flyout an editor opens adds a capturing `pointerdown` listener on window (`_flyDocDown`, here and in openFlyout at 4668). The listener is an arrow function over `this`, and neither close() (3206-3209 removes only the key listeners) nor destroy() (25299) removes it. A closed tab's editor therefore stays reachable for the rest of the session, with its layers, base, selection, mask caches and `flatCanvas`. On tiles the arena slots are freed only when the tile objects are collected, so they are never freed.
scenario: At 15,000 x 10,000 the user right-clicks a layer row (openLayerMenu, which opens a flyout) or opens a filter's choice list, then closes the tab. The base plus one full-size layer (more than 1.2 GB of tiles, plus a 572 MB flatCanvas if a filter layer was drawn) is never freed. After a few such tabs the renderer runs out of memory and ends, losing any unsaved work in the other tabs. The same class of leak was already fixed for the tip picker (8c14eee).
fix: In close() (or destroy()): `if (this._flyDocDown) { window.removeEventListener("pointerdown", this._flyDocDown, true); this._flyDocDown = null; }`. Or register it with an AbortController signal that destroy() aborts.
why: Confirmed. `_flyDocDown` is added to window as a capturing pointerdown listener in openFlyout (4663-4669) and openChoiceList (19618-19626), and is never removed: the only matches in the file are those adds. close() (3191-3233) removes only _docKey and _docKeyUp, and destroy() (25299-25311) does not touch it. The arrow function captures `this`, so a closed tab's editor stays reachable from window together with its layers, base, sel and caches. Tile slots go back to the arena only through a FinalizationRegistry when the tile objects are collected (inpaint_arena.js:10, 112), and closeDocument/removeEditor release nothing explicitly (shell.js:288-294, host.js:806-835). openFlyout runs on a tool group's long press or right-click (inpaint_modal.js:247-252) and on the layer row menu (13330), so almost every used tab leaks its whole document on close. At 15k that is GBs per tab, and the renderer ends after a few. Autosave limits what is lost, but this is a crash on a common path.

claim: The Canvas 2D path and the tiles program treat a plain filter layer differently. The Canvas 2D path is the screen whenever a filter layer is shown, and every flatten on the canvas backend. There applyFilterLayer draws the result source-over onto the canvas that still holds the filter's own input (:16314-16316), and flushFilterChain does the same with a chained surface (:16330). The tiles export/run program replaces the band with the result instead (programFinish :8814, `st.plain`). Every filter keeps its input's alpha (the shader writes `s.a`; an identity filter returns a copy, inpaint_filters_gl.js:1196), so the Canvas 2D path composites F(I) over I and raises the alpha of every half-transparent pixel.
scenario: Open a PNG cutout on a transparent canvas whose soft edges have alpha 128, then add a Curves layer at its defaults. curvesToTables returns null, so the layer is a copy. On screen the edge pixels go to alpha 192, and the canvas-backend export does the same. A Black & white layer instead gives the edges 2/3 grey + 1/3 of the original colour at alpha 192. Two filter layers that do not chain (a Vignette or Sharpen between them, or a pass above CHAIN_MAX_PIXELS) give alpha 239. The PNG exported on the tiles backend, and the picture a run sends, keep alpha 128 and pure grey. So the screen, the tiles export, the canvas export, and chained vs unchained passes all disagree on transparent documents. composite_test's FILTER_CHAIN step runs on an opaque document, and blendmodes covers half-transparent bases only for pixel layers.
fix: Make the program's rule the only rule: a plain filter layer stands for the picture. In applyFilterLayer, when `plain` (and only then: limitView, fills, masks, opacity, blends and clips keep source-over), clear [rx, ry, rw, rh] on ctx under its current transform before the drawImage of the result. Equivalently, draw with 'copy' inside a clip of that rectangle. Do the same in flushFilterChain before drawSurfaceTo, because a chain surface is always the result of plain filters. Add a gate step on a half-transparent base (alpha 128 edges) with an identity Curves layer and with a B&W layer. Compare the screen, flattenToCanvas on both backends, the plain PNG band export and an export with a Size row: all must give the same bytes, and the identity case must equal the base.
why:
The code shows it. The tiles program replaces the band for a plain filter step: `if (st.plain) { ... gpu = out; continue; }` at inpaint_canvas.js:8814, where plain means no mask, alpha 255, no op, no clip and not a fill (:8612). The Canvas 2D path does something else. drawLayersInto draws the layers below into ctx, and the screen view canvas or flatCanvas is cleared first, so a transparent base stays transparent. applyFilterLayer then draws the result with source-over onto that same canvas (:16314-16316). flushFilterChain also draws a chained surface source-over (:16330-16333). Every filter keeps the alpha it was given: the built-in shader writes `o = vec4(..., s.a)` (inpaint_filters_gl.js:140), and a no-op filter returns copyCanvas(src) (:1196). filteredCanvas has no no-op shortcut. So a pixel of alpha a ends at a + a(1-a), and its colour mixes F(I) with I: alpha 128 becomes 192, and a B&W layer gives 2/3 grey + 1/3 the original colour.

The defect reaches files as well as the screen, also on the default tiles backend. glCompositeUsable returns false whenever a filter layer is shown (:21705), so the screen always uses Canvas 2D. host.exportCanvas calls editor.flattenToCanvas (host.js:1016), and flattenToCanvas uses drawComposite, the Canvas 2D path (:22704-22712). That covers every non-plain export (a Size row, a Canvas frame), the PSD/ORA composite and JPEG/WebP. A plain PNG export (bandSource, then programBand) and a run's crop (readBoxBytes, how 'program') use the program and keep alpha 128. One document therefore exports differently with and without a Size row, and differently from the screen. composite_test's FILTER_CHAIN runs on an opaque gradient base (composite_test.py:46-58), and no test puts a filter layer over a half-transparent base. It is not in verified.json or BUGS.md, and none of tonight's branches touch it. must stands: an exported file gets wrong pixels on a transparent document (cutouts, transparent Generate new results).

claim: autosave.json, settings.json and secrets.json are each written as a temp file renamed over the old one, with no fsync (autosave.js:31-36, settings.js:78-83, keys.js:22-27). The .scumble writer and filesaves do fsync before their rename (docfile.js:501). Each of these readers also takes any read or parse error as an empty store, not only ENOENT (autosave.readJson; settings.readJson, settings.js:70-76; keys.readAll, keys.js:18-20), and settings.get() caches that. So the next write makes the loss permanent, and for keys and settings a transient read error is enough.
scenario: (1) A BSOD (for example a GPU driver hang while ComfyUI fills the card) or a power cut hits a few seconds after an autosave tick, which comes about every 15 s while the user edits. NTFS journals the rename and the new size but not the file data, so autosave.json can come back at the right length as zero bytes. At the next start readJson returns null. rotate() leaves generation 1 at the state from the start of the lost session. The window restores nothing, and its first autosave writes an empty session over the file. All unsaved work since the last app start is unreachable; the layer files sit unnamed in the mirror until a Clean up deletes them. A zeroed settings.json reads as {}, and the next settings.set writes the defaults over it (every window close writes `window`): the ComfyUI URL, recent documents and recipe picks are lost. A zeroed secrets.json makes keys.set store only the new key. (2) secrets.json cannot be read once: a sharing violation from a sync tool on a portable copy's data folder. The user saves one key: set() reads {} and writes { thatKey }, and every other provider key is gone. In settings.js:93-115 the first get() of the process caches DEFAULTS, and the first set() overwrites the user's settings.json with defaults: the ComfyUI URL, the chosen recipe, recipeLoras, recentDocuments, pluginData, the LLM rows and the helper links. Nothing tells the user.
fix: In the three writeJson helpers, fsync the temp file before renameSync (openSync, writeSync, fsyncSync, closeSync). Map only ENOENT to an empty store. On any other read or parse error, keep the file: rename it to <name>.damaged (or <name>.bad-<time>), log a warning, and either refuse the write (keys) or keep running on defaults without persisting until a later read succeeds (settings). Optionally keep a <name>.bak to fall back to.
why: Found from two slices. documents verifier: confirmed. autosave.writeJson (autosave.js:31-36), settings.writeJson (settings.js:78-83), keys.writeAll (keys.js:22-27) and docfile writeList all call writeFileSync and then renameSync with no fsync. docfile's own writer does fsync before its rename (docfile.js:501), and PLAN_DOCUMENTS.md:104 only claims that a kill leaves the old file whole, not a power loss. After a crash, NTFS can show a renamed file at its new length filled with zeros. Every reader then takes the parse error as an empty store: autosave readJson returns null, settings returns {}, keys returns {}. The next write makes the loss final: an empty session autosave, the defaults written on the next settings.set (the window bounds are written on every close), and a keys.set that stores only the new key. The mirror's layer files are also written without fsync (files.js:89), so this fix protects the stores but not the pixels. main verifier (rated nice): the pattern is in the code; keys.js:18-20 readAll and settings.js:70-76 readJson map every read or parse error to {} or DEFAULTS, get() caches that (settings.js:93-110), and the next set() writes the whole object back, so one transient read error at the first read wipes every key or every setting. In the torn case the data is already gone, so the catch-all adds harm only for transient errors (a sharing violation, EIO). Both triggers are rare. Kept at should: it is a quit-safety and autosave path, the loss is silent, and the fix is small.

claim: When the MCP client closes stdin, the launcher ends the child's stdin and kills the Electron app 5 s later, whatever the app is doing. An own (headless) instance quits on that EOF through the normal close path, and that path waits up to 120 s for the window to save. The kill cuts the save short.
scenario: No Scumble is running. Claude Code / Desktop starts `Scumble --mcp` through launch.js, which starts the app headless. The agent edits a 15k document: paints, merges, dodge/burn, a result layer. Layer pixels reach the mirror only 15 s after the last change. The session then ends with a normal stdin close. launch.js:77-83 clientGone calls child.stdin.end(), and the child's serve() sees the end. onClose (main.js:1511-1515) calls maybeQuit -> app.quit -> win 'close' -> quitGuard.run(flushAll), where saveBeforeRestart syncs each dirty layer (a PNG encode plus upload, about 1.5-3 s per 15k layer) and then the bundle. With two or more dirty layers the flush takes more than 5 s, so `child.kill()` (TerminateProcess on Windows) ends it midway. The agent's last edits are missing at the next start. The same happens to edits the user made in that instance's window: in agentMode a close only hides the window, so its save is put off to this flush (main.js:373). The launcher's other path is safer: when the client kills the launcher itself, nothing kills the child, and the child saves fully.
fix: Spawn the child with detached: true in launch.js:52 (keep windowsHide and the stdio pipes), so it survives the launcher and is outside its job object, and finishes its flush on stdin EOF. Drop the 5 s kill in clientGone, or raise it past FLUSH_TIMEOUT (about 130 s). Keep the kill for SIGTERM/SIGINT of the launcher only when the child is a proxy. Make the same change in mcpb/server/index.js:246-247. Add a gate step: a headless MCP session that ends right after a paint edit on a large canvas, then the layer is checked in the mirror or autosave at the next start.
why: The code shows it. launch.js:77-82 ends the child's stdin and calls child.kill() 5 s later. The timer is unref'd, but the child's pipes keep the loop alive, so it still fires. In the child, stdin's end (mcp/server.js:157-160) calls onClose, which sets agentMode to null and calls maybeQuit (main.js:1426-1428, 1510-1515). That leads to app.quit, the window 'close', and quitGuard.run(flushAll('quit')) with a timeout of up to 120 s (quit.js FLUSH_TIMEOUT). The flush syncs every dirty layer (shell.js:2893-2925 saveBeforeRestart, inpaint_canvas.js:22948 syncLayersOnce). A 15k document with 4 layers took 2.9 s to flush (docs/measurements/w0b_2026-10-23/once/gates/gates/docperf/docperf.log, flushMs 2883), so two or more dirty 15k layers plus the selection encode can go past 5 s and be TerminateProcess'd. Every write is tmp+rename, so nothing is corrupted. What is lost is the edits of the last ~15 s before the stdin close. That makes it should, not must: it needs an agent-owned headless instance and a session that ends within ~15 s of the last edit at 15k. Correction to the claim (inferred from libuv's Windows spawn, not measured): the 'safer' path is not safe either. libuv puts children spawned without detached into its own KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job, so a client that kills the launcher (the MCP TS SDK's close: stdin end, then SIGTERM after about 2 s) also kills the Electron child mid-flush. mcpb/server/index.js:246-247 has the same 5 s kill of the launcher. Not in verified.json or BUGS.md.

claim: The window's close handler writes the window bounds through settings.set() before it calls e.preventDefault() and starts the save-before-close. settings.js writeJson is a bare writeFileSync plus renameSync, with no retry. On Windows the rename fails with EPERM/EBUSY when another program holds settings.json, and the project already retries for that elsewhere (docfile.js BUSY / renameRetry). If it throws, the listener aborts, the close is not prevented, and the window closes without the flush.
scenario: An antivirus, indexer or backup tool has settings.json open when the user closes the window. settings.set -> fs.renameSync throws EPERM, which log.js only records as 'uncaught'. Lines 373-386 never run: no quitGuard.run(flushAll), and the layers edited in the last ~15 s plus the final autosave are never written. The window closes at once and the app quits. The same unguarded settings.set runs on every agentMode close and in addRecent after every document save. There the throw turns a document save that succeeded into an IPC error.
fix: Wrap the bounds write at main.js:368-370 in try/catch, or move it after the quitGuard decision. Wrap addRecent's settings.set in try/catch at the documents:write and documents:open handlers. Give settings.js, keys.js and autosave.js writeJson a short synchronous busy retry (EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES, docfile.BUSY), the way renameRetry does it.
why: Confirmed. main.js:368-370 calls settings.set() before the agentMode check and before e.preventDefault(). settings.js:78-83 writeJson is writeFileSync+renameSync, with no try and no retry. A throw from the listener goes to log.js:140's uncaughtException handler, the close is not prevented, and the window closes without quitGuard.run(flushAll). The edits of the last ~15 s and the final autosave are lost. Rename failures of a freshly written tmp on Windows (an AV scan holding the tmp, a sync tool) are a known class: the project retries them itself in docfile.js:193/400 renameRetry. The same unguarded set in addRecent (main.js:889-896) runs after documents.write has succeeded (1123-1126), so a save that worked is reported as failed. The trigger is rare and transient, but this is a quit-safety path and the fix is tiny.

claim: Generate new can run on an empty tab, and that tab stays free for any file the user opens while the request is out. When the answer lands it replaces whatever the tab holds by then. openDocument reuses the active tab when `!cur.base && !cur._loading && !cur.docFile` (host.js:6112), and openInto reuses it when `!ed.base` (renderer/shell.js:319). Neither checks `providerPending`. runGenerate then calls `setBaseFromCanvas(c, { keepRefs: true })` (host.js:2976) without checking that the tab still holds the picture it was asked for. setBaseFromCanvas drops every layer except the references and clears the history, the selections, the maps and the undo stack (inpaint_canvas.js:21130-21142).
scenario: 1. New tab, Generate new with FLUX 3 (20-60 s). 2. While it waits, the user opens a .scumble from File > Open or Explorer. openDocument picks the empty, active, generating tab and restores the document into it. 3. The answer lands: the document's layers, history and undo are gone and the generated picture becomes the base. 4. The tab still has the .scumble as its docFile and the file on disk is unchanged, so Ctrl+S (or Close > Save) writes the generated picture over the .scumble without any question. The original layers are now lost on disk too. The same happens with a PNG opened (Ctrl+O, drop) into that tab and edited for a while: the edits and their undo are wiped.
fix: In openDocument's `reuse` and shell.js openInto, also skip a tab where `ed.providerPending || (host.runsOf && host.runsOf(ed).length)` and open a new tab instead. In runGenerate, note `editor.base` and `editor.docFile` before the first await. If either has changed when the answer is in, do not call setBaseFromCanvas on that tab: land the picture in a new tab (or refuse with a red line), then endRun.
why: The code shows it. generate_new has no needsImage, so runGenerate's API route runs on a tab with no base and sets only providerPending. The Generate new dialog can be closed with Escape while the run goes on (its cancel handler only intercepts popups), and an MCP generate_new opens no dialog at all. openDocument's reuse test (host.js:6112: !cur.base && !cur._loading && !_rawStates.has(cur) && !cur.docFile) and shell.js openInto (317-320: `if (!ed || ed.base)`) never look at providerPending or runsOf. restore() sets ed.docFile and setValue loads the document into the generating tab. When the answer lands, runGenerate calls setBaseFromCanvas(c, {keepRefs:true}) (host.js:2976) without comparing base or docFile with the click. setBaseFromCanvas (inpaint_canvas.js:21122-21142) empties the layers, history, savedSelections, maps and sel, and calls clearUndo. Nothing clears docFile (it is only ever set, at host.js:1479 and 6071). On Ctrl+S, saveDocument (6016ff) saves in place without a question when the stat is unchanged. Downgraded from must to should: it needs a file opened into a tab that is visibly running a job (busy dot, 'Asking ... for a new image'). The in-memory loss is limited to edits made during the run. The .scumble on disk is lost only if the user saves after seeing the wrong picture.

claim: openGeneration (Settings › Local files › Earlier states, the recovery path after a crash) rebuilds each document as { id, state } only. The bundle's per-document `plugins` (pluginData) and `extra` are dropped, and host.restore then sets pluginData to {} and docExtra to {} (host.js:1480-1481). reopenClosed passes both (host.js:6181).
scenario: Scumble crashes twice while restoring, and the start line points to Earlier states. The user opens the state there. The documents come back without their prompt boxes (Boxes plugin) and without the glb plugin's 3D-object data, so the 3D layers can no longer be edited. A newer document's unknown fields are gone too. Every later open of that state drops them again, so the UI offers no way to get them back. No test covers openGeneration.
fix: fresh = docs.map((d) => ({ id: host.nextId++, state: d.state, plugins: d.plugins, extra: d.extra })), leaving the file out on purpose as now. Add a gate step that opens a generation holding a box.
why: Confirmed. openGeneration (renderer/shell.js:2407-2417) maps each doc to { id, state } only. host.restore then sets pluginData = {} and docExtra = {} when doc.plugins / doc.extra are missing (host.js:1480-1481). The autosave bundle carries both per doc (docMeta, host.js:216-222). The Boxes plugin (plugins/boxes/main.js:37-38) and glb (plugins/glb/main.js:36-59) keep their data in documents.data, i.e. pluginData. A document opened from Earlier states therefore loses its prompt boxes and its 3D objects' data. reopenClosed (host.js:6181) and openDocument (:6115) pass both. Severity lowered from must: pixels and layers come back, and the generation file on disk is not changed. What is lost is plugin data in the reopened copy, with no UI to get it back.

claim: rememberClosed (called from shell.js closeDocument:293 without waiting for its flush) puts the state captured BEFORE flushEditor on the closed list. reopenClosed pops that entry at once, and getValue stores only each layer's `ref`. A tab reopened while the flush still runs therefore comes back with the last uploaded pixels; the fresh capture after the flush finds its entry gone and is dropped.
scenario: The user paints on an existing layer and on a new paint layer, presses Ctrl+W within about 15 s (layers upload 15 s after the last change), answers 'Don't Save', then presses Ctrl+Shift+T. An agent's close_document followed by reopen_closed_tab does the same. The reopened tab shows the old layer's previous pixels and an empty new layer. At 15000 x 10000 the window is longer, because the upload itself takes seconds.
fix: Keep the flush promise on the closed entry, and have reopenClosed await it, bounded by the same 30 s, before it restores. Alternatively, push a pending placeholder that the reopen waits for and capture after the flush.
why: Confirmed. rememberClosed (renderer/editor/host.js:6153-6171) pushes the state it captures before flushEditor. It replaces that entry after the flush only if the entry is still in the list (indexOf >= 0). reopenClosed (:6174-6181) pops the newest entry at once, with no wait. getValue writes each layer's stored ref (inpaint_canvas.js:24699), so a dirty layer's pixels that are not yet uploaded are not in the captured state. Ctrl+W, Don't Save, then Ctrl+Shift+T during the flush (seconds at 15k) brings the tab back with the last uploaded pixels. The fresh capture is then dropped, and the closed editor is destroyed. An agent hits this more easily: close_document does not await closeDocument (commands.js:970), so a following reopen_closed_tab always runs during the flush.

claim: The rule that text layers hold text, not pixels, exists only in `patchRefusal` (10086), `shapeTarget` (11493) and Remove. The brush and eraser, gradient, smudge/tone, clone/heal (pointer-down near 6264-6398), `bucketFill`, `fillSelection` (12314) and `clearSelectedPixels` (12449) write straight into a text layer's `px`. `renderTextLayer` replaces `px` from the text description on the next edit (17440), and nothing converts the layer to paint first, unlike distort/warp (3035-3043).
scenario: Add a text layer, erase part of a letter or paint over it with the brush or bucket, then change the font size or fix a typo. The paint and erase work disappear without a word. They come back only by undoing the text edit.
fix: Use one check for every pixel tool on a text layer. Either refuse with the existing 'Text layers hold text, not pixels' line, or turn the layer into a paint layer under a `layers` undo step first, as distort and warp do (3035-3043).
why: Confirmed. The text-layer refusal exists only in `patchRefusal` (10086) and `shapeTarget` (11493). The paint/erase branch (6369-6391), smudge/tone (6264-6303), clone/heal (6304-6332), the gradient (6355-6365), `bucketFill` (11734-11760), `fillSelection` (12314) and `clearSelectedPixels` (12449) check only locked and filter layers, then write into a text layer's `px`. Nothing turns the layer into a paint layer; only distort and warp do (3035-3043). `renderTextLayer` (17413-17455) replaces `layer.px` with a fresh render of the description on the next text edit, font change or document turn (5366), so the paint disappears without a word. The text undo step still holds the painted pixels, so only an undo brings them back.

claim: newCanvas empties `this.layers`, `history`, `savedSelections`, `maps`, `guides` and `compare` and sets `this.sel = null` before calling setBasePixels. setBasePixels then throws its Each-area refusal (18463). The catch only writes a status line, so the document keeps its old base with no layers and a null selection. setBaseFromCanvas (21131-21141) has the same order.
scenario: Each area (item 54) is running on a tab, e.g. four areas on an API. An agent or the assistant calls `new_canvas` on that tab; the command checks neither busy() nor _eachArea. Every layer and the results history vanish, and the status says 'Could not create the canvas: Each area is running...'. From then on pushUndo returns early (`!this.sel`), so no new step can be taken. Code that reads `this.sel` throws TypeErrors. The next autosave stores the document with `layers: []`.
fix: Check `this._eachArea` (and the setBasePixels size check) at the top of newCanvas and setBaseFromCanvas, before any reset. Or move the resets into setBasePixels after its own checks.
why: Confirmed. newCanvas (inpaint_canvas.js:21332-21342) sets layers=[], history=[], savedSelections=[], maps={}, guides, compare and sel=null before `await this.setBasePixels(...)`. setBasePixels' first line throws the Each-area refusal (18463), and the catch (21371-21372) only writes the status. setBaseFromCanvas (21130-21141) has the same order. Neither the editor's New button (inpaint_modal.js:99) nor the MCP new_canvas command (commands.js:1113-1130, no busy check outside the assistant's refuseBusy) checks _eachArea, and busy() (shell.js:192) does not include it. Result: the old base with no layers, sel null (so pushUndo returns early at 14388), and an autosave with layers []. The status reads as a clean refusal. Downgraded to should: the caller meant to discard anyway, and the trigger is narrow (New during a running Each area).

claim: importFile takes a workflow's or API prompt's recipe id from the file name (slug(stem)) and saves <id>.json in the user folder with no check for an id that already exists. Only flux2_klein_local is protected (1882). An existing user recipe with that id is overwritten without a word, and any other shipped recipe with that id is hidden behind the import, because list() prefers user recipes. The two other ways a recipe is made pick a fresh id against the taken ones: fromGraph's 'Save as new recipe' (1278-1283) and the Comfy Cloud import branch (1856-1857, which passes ids).
scenario: The user imports ~/Downloads/workflow.json, ComfyUI's default export name, and gets recipe 'workflow'. Later they import a different graph that was also exported as workflow.json. save() rewrites userDir/workflow.json, so the first recipe is gone from Scumble, along with any edits saved into it from the ComfyUI window. Its stored LoRA rows and presets (settings.recipeLoras / recipePresets, keyed by id) now apply to the new graph. A second case: importing a workflow named relight.json hides the shipped 'relight' provider recipe. host.relightWhole looks up exactly that id, so relight would then get a ComfyUI edit graph.
fix: For stem-derived ids (the fromWorkflow / fromPrompt branches), pick a fresh id against list()'s ids (stem_2, stem_3 ...), as fromCloudGraph and fromGraph already do. Then name the id actually used in the import note. A Scumble recipe file (data.kind) whose id is already a user recipe can keep its replace semantics, but should say 'replaced <id>' in the note.
why: Confirmed in the snapshot. In electron/main/recipes.js:1879, importFile sets recipe.id = slug(stem) for a UI workflow or API prompt that holds an Inpaint Canvas node (the fromWorkflow / fromPrompt branches, data.kind unset). save() (852-857) then writes userDir/<id>.json with a plain fsp.writeFile and no existence check. Only flux2_klein_local is renamed (1882). Neither the IPC handler (main.js:938-956) nor shell.js importRecipe (759-776) asks before replacing, and the note just says 'Imported "name"'. list() (838-843) prefers user recipes over shipped ones. The Comfy Cloud branch (1855-1857) and fromGraph do pass the taken ids and pick a fresh one. The scenario holds: a second canvas workflow imported under the same file stem (from another folder or machine, or after the first file was moved) replaces the first user recipe, including any edits saved into it from the ComfyUI window. The id-keyed LoRA rows and presets then apply to the other graph. Two caveats lower the likelihood but not the defect. A browser saves a duplicate download as 'workflow (1).json', which slugs to a different id. And shadowing a shipped id is documented as intended for recipe files (docs/RECIPES.md 619-620), so the relight half of the scenario is by design. The silent loss of a user recipe is not. Not in verified.json: S9a is only about sanitising the id in save. Not in BUGS.md Open, and not part of H1's 'recipe ids as file names'.

claim: ToAPIs' setPath() walks dotted keys with no guard. A key that starts with "__proto__." therefore writes onto Object.prototype in the main process. The keys come from recipe data: every params key (toapis.js:314-317, which come from the recipe's settings[].key and fixed keys through host.providerParams) and the recipe options tier_key, seed and negative (325-327). recipes.importFile takes a provider recipe as it is (recipes.js:1865 `recipe = { ...data }`) and does not check settings keys. The project treats recipes as untrusted elsewhere: openrouter.js:462 refuses "__proto__" slugs, and toapis.js:39 says an imported recipe could send the key anywhere.
scenario: The user imports a shared recipe file whose toapis variant has fixed: {"__proto__.method": "DELETE"} or {"__proto__.nodeIntegration": true}, or a settings row with key "__proto__.x". The user has a ToAPIs key stored and runs it once. bodyFor calls setPath(body, "__proto__.method", ...), so every object in main now inherits that property. Every later fetch init without its own method then sends that method. Inferred worst case, not verified: an options object Electron reads with prototype lookups (webPreferences of the next WebContentsView, e.g. the ComfyUI window) picks up nodeIntegration and gives a remote page Node. At the least, main misbehaves process-wide until restart.
fix: In setPath and getPath, refuse any segment that is __proto__, constructor or prototype, or does not match /^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/ (throw "... nothing was sent"). Descend only into own properties (Object.hasOwn). Also validate provider-variant settings[].key, fixed keys and the dotted option keys (tier_key, seed, negative) in recipes.normalize with the same pattern, so no adapter ever sees such a key. Add a unit test where the __proto__ key is refused and ({}).method stays undefined.
why: Confirmed. In toapis.js:115-123, setPath(body, "__proto__.method", v) finds o["__proto__"] truthy, an object and not an array, steps into Object.prototype and assigns there. The keys reach it unchecked from recipe data. host.js:2076-2081 providerParams copies settings[].key and the variant's fixed keys as own properties, IPC keeps them, index.js:254 passes request.params on, and toapis.js:314-317 loops over them. tier_key, seed and negative (325-327) come from options. recipes.importFile (1863-1865) takes a provider recipe as it is, and normalize (758-790) never checks setting or fixed keys. Tonight's H1 covers recipe ids as file names, not this. I lowered the severity from must: it needs a crafted recipe that the user imports and then runs on ToAPIs with a stored key. The proven effect is that main misbehaves process-wide until a restart (for example, every later fetch init without its own method inherits it). The escalation to webPreferences is plausible but not verified.

claim: policy.layerBelow assumes list_layers answers top first, but list_layers returns ed.layers bottom first (commands.js:1979; mergeDown takes layers[i - 1] as below). The merge_down row therefore checks the layer ABOVE the target, so the assistant merges into the user's layer or into the base image without asking. prompt.js:72 also labels the same list 'top first' for the model, and its 1.5 kB cut drops the top (newest) layers.
scenario: Base plus the user's layer U, then the assistant generates R1 and R2 (both owned; list_layers gives [U, R1, R2]). merge_down {layer: R1}: layerBelow returns R2, which is owned, so the row says AUTO and the editor merges R1 into U, the user's layer, with no card. With only R1 and R2 above the base, merge_down R1 is AUTO and merges into the base image, which the row means to ask for. merge_down on the top layer asks with the wrong reason ('into the base image'). The model also reads the stack upside down, so 'the top layer' means the bottom one. The test fixture (tools/assistant_test.js:1224) lists layers top first, so it hides this.
fix: policy.layerBelow: return at > 0 ? list[at - 1] : null, so the bottom layer gives 'into the base image' (ASK). prompt.stateNote: say 'bottom first', or reverse the list, and keep the top entries when cutting. Reorder the assistant_test.js facts fixture to bottom-first and add the U/R1/R2 merge_down case.
why: Confirmed. list_layers returns ed.layers bottom to top (renderer/commands.js:1979), and mergeDownNow merges into this.layers[i - 1] (renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:17224-17225). policy.js:221-227 still reads list[at + 1] with the comment 'top first', so the merge_down row (policy.js:101-105) judges the layer ABOVE the target. Base + U (the user's) + R1, R2 (owned): merge_down R1 is AUTO and merges R1 into U. With only R1 and R2 above the base, merge_down R1 is AUTO and merges into the base, which the row means to ask for. stateNote (prompt.js:72) also labels the bottom-first list 'top first', and its 1.4 kB cut keeps the bottom entries. The test fixture (tools/assistant_test.js:1224-1229) is ordered as if top first. Not listed in verified.json or BUGS.md. Severity lowered to should: it skips a consent question for a merge that Ctrl+Z / Undo this turn can take back. It is not a security hole and loses no data.

claim: A paid provider run (fal, OpenAI, BFL, Gemini, Replicate, WaveSpeed, OpenRouter, ToAPIs, Magnific ...) whose page reloads or crashes during the run is charged, and main throws its picture away. Only Comfy Cloud jobs come back after a page goes away (`pageGone` is read only when ctx.jobNote is set, providers/index.js:325). View > Reload (reloadWindow, main.js:488-496) neither waits for running provider runs nor asks about them.
scenario: The user starts a GPT Image / FLUX 3 edit on a 15k picture that takes 40-90 s, then presses Ctrl+R (or the renderer crashes and CrashGuard reloads it, main.js:405-421). main's ipcMain.handle('provider:edit') keeps running providers.edit and receives the bytes, and the log says '<provider> edit ok in N s'. The reply goes to an invoke whose page is gone, and Electron drops it. The new page has no record of the run, nothing is in the mirror, and the paid picture is gone.
fix: In providers.edit, after a successful run with hooks.pageGone() true and no jobNote, write out.bytes to <userData>/results/<runId>.<ext>. Add a note through cloudjobs (or a sibling list) of the form { runId, recipe, model, provider, started, file }, and call jobsChanged, so the new page's existing ask (recoverCloudResults) opens it as a document. In reloadWindow, ask first while providers' running map is not empty ('N paid runs are still going; their pictures are kept if you reload').
why: Confirmed. main.js:1181-1188 passes hooks.pageGone, but providers/index.js:323 reads it only when ctx.jobNote is set, which only Comfy Cloud v2 sets. For fal, OpenAI, BFL, Gemini, Replicate, WaveSpeed, OpenRouter, ToAPIs and Magnific, the bytes come back, the log records '<label> edit ok', and the result is returned to an invoke whose frame has navigated away. Nothing writes it anywhere. View > Reload (Ctrl+R, main.js:743, reloadWindow 488-496) flushes but never looks at running provider runs. The CrashGuard reload (405-421) and did-start-navigation (389-402) do not either. Not in BUGS.md or verified.json. The S6 plan scoped recovery to Comfy Cloud (docs/PLAN_COMFY_SDK.md S6). This is should, not must: it needs a manual reload or a renderer crash during the run, and one run costs cents to about a dollar. Both are plausible at 15k, though: the window looks stuck during a 60-90 s run, and renderer OOMs are known there.

claim: At turn:done (Stop, error, reset), the panel only unpins unanswered ask cards (releaseAsk): their Allow and Don't buttons stay enabled and their state still says 'waiting for you'. Main's answer(callId) matches by call id alone, and call ids repeat across steps: Gemini uses `call_${i}` when functionCall has no id (gemini.js:279), and chat.js uses `call_${n + 1}` for servers that send none. A click on a stale card can therefore answer a different, newer ask.
scenario: A Gemini chat. Step one asks close_document as call_0, and the user presses Stop (main counts this as a decline). Card A stays clickable. The next turn asks generate each_area on fal, also as call_0 (card B). The user clicks Allow on card A: answer('call_0', true) resolves B's pending ask, and up to 8 paid runs start that the user never allowed.
fix: On turn:done, Stop and reset, disable the buttons of every unanswered ask card and set its state to 'not answered'. Give each ask a unique token (a turn id plus a counter) that the card sends back, and have answer() accept only the pending token.
why: Confirmed. On turn:done the panel only calls releaseAsk (renderer/assistant.js:543). releaseAsk (skins.js:362-375) removes the popover pinning but leaves the buttons enabled and the state text 'waiting for you'. Their click handlers call answer(e.call, ...) (assistant.js:448-449, 481-489). Main's answer() matches by callId alone (electron/main/assistant/index.js:277-283). Stop resolves the pending ask as false (:272), and a stale card stays clickable. Call ids repeat across steps when the server sends none: gemini.js:279 uses `call_${i}` and chat.js:333 uses `call_${n+1}`. A click on a stale card can therefore resolve a newer pending ask with the same id, for example a paid each_area generate. With unique ids, the stale click does nothing in main but marks the card 'allowed'. The collision depends on the provider leaving ids out, which the code's own fallback expects.

claim: The render card's settings and the chat's changes are never filled: facts.recipe reads chat.recipe and facts.changedByChat reads chat.changedSettings, which nothing ever sets, and facts.settings, mode and queue are never set either. The generate / generate_new / upscale card therefore names only the recipe. The policy table (docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:2644) still makes set_settings, apply_preset and set_generation AUTO because 'the render card lists the settings and marks the ones this chat changed'. A5's notes record this record as not built.
scenario: On an API recipe, the chat AUTO-runs set_settings {quality: 'high', size: '4K'} or apply_preset, then calls generate. The ask card shows only 'recipe: GPT Image 2.6', so the user allows a run at a tier several times the price without being shown the change the chat just made.
fix: Record per document which rows set_settings, apply_preset and set_generation changed. For generate, generate_new and upscale, read list_settings into facts.settings so the card shows them, marked 'this chat set it'. Until then, make set_settings and apply_preset ASK on provider recipes.
why: Confirmed. factsFor reads chat.recipe and chat.changedSettings (electron/main/assistant/index.js:847-848), and nothing in electron/main/assistant/ ever sets them. facts.settings, mode and queue are never set. So renderCard (policy.js:265-274) carries only nulls, and the panel shows only the recipe from host.recipe (renderer/assistant.js:466-469). Meanwhile set_settings, apply_preset and set_generation are AUTO (policy.js:61-63), on the policy table's stated condition that the render card lists the settings and marks the chat's changes (docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:2644, 2658). A5's notes (PLAN_ASSISTANT.md:2040-2043) record the record as not built, but it is not in BUGS.md's Open list or verified.json. The planned test a_changed_setting_is_shown_on_the_render_card does not exist in tools/. A chat can therefore raise an API recipe's tier or size and get a generate approved that shows only the recipe name. The reads of never-set fields are also dead code that misleads.

claim: On fal and Replicate, a Cancel, and also the adapter's own 15/30-minute timeout, only stop Scumble from waiting. Neither asks the provider to stop. Yet fal's submit answer carries cancel_url (PUT; a request still IN_QUEUE is dropped and not billed), and a Replicate prediction carries urls.cancel (POST; stops a time-billed run, and an official model cancelled before its output is not billed). Comfy Cloud and Comfy Router got exactly this (comfysdk.cancelJob, comfyrouter send/lastLook). Replicate, WaveSpeed and BFL also wait between polls with util.sleep instead of ctx.sleep, so a Cancel waits out the pause.
scenario: At a busy hour the user queues a fal Topaz upscale, sees it sit in the queue and presses Cancel (or the 30-minute wait runs out while it is still queued). index.js says "Scumble stopped waiting for fal.ai, which may still finish the job and charge it". The request stays in fal's queue, runs later and is billed, though a single PUT would have dropped it for free. On Replicate, a cancelled long prediction keeps running and billing to the end.
fix: Keep the cancel URL from the submit answer (only https on queue.fal.run or api.replicate.com). On ctx.signal abort and on the adapter's own timeout, send it once on a short request that is not bound to the run's signal (globalThis.fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(10000), as comfysdk.cancelJob does), and set ctx.cancelAsked from the answer so index.js words the Cancel right. Switch Replicate, WaveSpeed and BFL to (ctx.sleep || sleep).
why: Confirmed. No adapter in providers/ reads cancel_url or urls.cancel (grep finds nothing). fal's queued() keeps only status_url and response_url (246); PLAN_FLUX3.md:323 documents the PUT .../cancel route. Replicate's pred.urls is read for get only (205). An abort or the adapters' own 15/30-minute timeouts (fal.js:252, replicate.js:203, wavespeed.js:296) only stop the waiting. index.js:313 then says honestly that the provider may still finish and charge the job, so this is a missed saving more than a silent bug. On a timeout, a fal request still IN_QUEUE runs later, is billed, and is never fetched. replicate.js:204, wavespeed.js:297 and bfl.js:128/133/158 sleep with util.sleep, not ctx.sleep, so a Cancel waits out the rest of a 1-2 s pause; that part is trivial.

claim: Opening or reopening a document keeps the Settings rows saved with the recipe of that time, keyed only by row index. A run of the current recipe then sends those values into its own rows. settingsChanged (inpaint_canvas.js:24309) is the step that resets an entry whose `target` names another recipe. It runs only from applyRecipe and onConnected. restore() (host.js:1482), used by openDocument and reopenClosed, calls `ed.setValue()` and then `keepRecipeMode()` only, and setValue just assigns `state.settings`. providerParams (host.js:2077-2078) and queueGenerate (host.js:5570-5574) read `editor.settings[String(s.index)]` without comparing `entry.target`. This is the bug the comment at host.js:2045-2046 says the target keys fixed ("Klein was queued with Qwen's files", the ToAPIs channel); this path skips that fix.
scenario: A .scumble saved while 'Flux.2 Klein local' was selected is opened while 'Qwen Image Edit 2.1 local' is selected. The open's note says the recipes differ but does not switch the recipe. Generate queues the Qwen graph with Klein's UNet, CLIP and VAE in the same loader nodes. Both files exist on the server, so missingFilesRefusal passes, and the sampler fails or renders garbage. With API recipes, the old recipe's value for row k (a quality, a ToAPIs channel, a resolution such as 4K) goes out as the new recipe's row-k parameter on a paid run. The panel shows the old value under the old label, so it does not look wrong.
fix: After setValue in restore() (which covers openDocument and reopenClosed), call ed.settingsChanged() (or this.applyRecipe(ed)). Entries whose target matches the current recipe keep their values, the others go back to the recipe's defaults. As a net, providerParams and queueGenerate should skip an entry whose `target` is not the row's key (`${r.id}/${s.node}:${s.input}`).
why: Confirmed. setValue copies state.settings as it is (inpaint_canvas.js:24807). restore() follows it with keepRecipeMode only (host.js:1482), and keepRecipeMode's own comment says the Settings values stay as the file has them. settingsChanged, the only step that resets an entry whose target names another recipe, is called only from applyRecipe (host.js:2007, from addEditor before setValue and from setRecipe), onConnected (1435) and set_settings. providerParams (2077-2078) and queueGenerate (5570-5574) read editor.settings[String(s.index)] without comparing entry.target. The recipe files show the reviewer's exact case: flux2_klein_local and qwen_image_edit_2_1_local both have index 1/2/3 = unet/clip/vae unet_name/clip_name/vae_name, and index 6 is Klein's `megapixels` against Qwen's `resolution`. A Klein-saved document opened (or a tab reopened) while Qwen is selected therefore queues Klein's files, and its megapixels value as Qwen's resolution. The Settings panel does show the old values under the old labels, which softens the 'does not look wrong' part, but the run still goes out with them.

claim: An export's target path is one global, `host.exportPath`. commands.js withExportPath (3005-3008) sets it and restores the previous value in a finally. saveExport reads it only after the export's flatten, encode and awaits, which take seconds at 15k. Overlapping exports therefore write to each other's paths, and one interleaving leaves the path set for good. Exports are not serialized: bridge.js keeps many requests pending, and MCP clients issue tool calls in parallel.
scenario: (1) While the assistant or Claude Desktop runs `export` to C:\out\a.png on a 15k document, the user clicks Save in the Export section of any tab. The user's picture is written to a.png with no dialog, then the agent's export overwrites it, or the other way round. (2) Two parallel calls, `export` a.png and `export_mask` b.png. A sets the path to a, B sets it to b (its prev is a). A's saveExport now reads b and writes the picture to b.png. Then B overwrites b.png. a.png is never written. A's finally sets null, B's finally sets a. From then on every UI export in the session goes silently to a.png. (The parallel `export` command also races on the shared saveFormatSel and saveNameInput.)
fix: Pass the path with the call instead of through a global. Have saveExport(blob, name, { path }) take it, and have exportImage, exportLayerPng and exportMaskPng forward a path argument that the three commands give. Optionally run export commands one at a time per document, since `export` also writes the shared saveFormatSel and saveNameInput.
why: Confirmed. host.exportPath is one global field (host.js:599). withExportPath (commands.js:3005-3008) sets it and restores the previous value in a finally. saveExport reads it only when it reaches file.saveStart (host.js:5813), after the export's flatten and encode. Nothing serializes commands: shell.js onRequest calls commands.call directly for each request, commands.run awaits no lock, and bridge.js keeps a map of pending ids. The races hold. (1) A user's UI export that reaches saveExport while an agent's export with `path` is running writes to the agent's path with no dialog, and the agent's file then overwrites it, or the other way round. (2) For two overlapping path exports, one interleaving writes A's picture to B's path. Another (A finishes before B, so A's finally sets null and then B's finally sets A's path) leaves exportPath set for the rest of the session, so later UI exports go silently to that file. MCP clients issue parallel tool calls, so (2) is reachable.

claim: A local Generate whose `executed` event falls into a websocket gap never lands, and nothing says so. ComfyUI does not replay `executed` to a reconnected client. After main's reconnect (electron/main/comfy.js openSocket, 0.5-15 s backoff), the server's `status` (queue_remaining 0) clears every `_localRuns` (host.js:6956) and idles the bars. setServerStatus on the socket's return only re-checks the bars (checkTrackedRuns, host.js:696). Nothing reads /history for the document's prompts. Picture runs already have this fallback (comfyPictureRun -> pictureFromHistory); Generate results do not.
scenario: Remote ComfyUI (RunPod) and a 40 s Flux render. The socket drops for a few seconds while the result is written. The result file is in the server's output and in /history/<id> with `inpaint_result`, but no layer appears. The status line stays 'Queued crop ... Waiting for the result ...', the bar goes away, the user's paid GPU time is wasted, and the `generate` command ends with 'no result arrived'. Each area on ComfyUI stops with 'its prompt ended on your ComfyUI without a result'.
fix: When the socket comes back (st.socket true after false), take each editor's prompt ids it still expects (its _sentTexts keys and runProgress.dropped). For each id the queue no longer holds, read /history/<id>, hand outputs[*].inpaint_result to the same landing path as the `executed` listener (factor that body into a function), then markLanded. pictureFromHistory shows the shape. A poll of /history for those ids when the status says the queue is empty without an `executed` would also cover a missed event.
why: Confirmed. A Generate result lands only through the `executed` listener (host.js ~6900ff, out.inpaint_result into addResults). On reconnect, comfy.js openSocket uses the same clientId, but ComfyUI does not replay `executed`. The `status` listener (host.js:6954-6957) clears every _localRuns and idles the bars when queue_remaining is 0. setServerStatus on the socket's return only calls checkTrackedRuns (696), and that reads /queue for the bars, not /history. The only /history readers (pictureFromHistory, 3572) serve picture runs (Realism Pass, key, whole-picture upscale), never Generate. The generate command's loop breaks once the queue is idle and throws 'no result arrived' (commands.js 1911-1924). The result sits in the server's output folder and in /history but never becomes a layer. This is not in BUGS.md and not part of tonight's work.

claim: cropCanvasNow (5985), resizeImageNow (6046) and extendCanvasNow (13943) take their canvas snapshot, then await the base's encode and upload, then commit. They never re-check what happened during the wait. turnDocumentNow (5340-5348) and straightenDocumentNow do re-check: historyGen, basePx, size, gestureHeld, turnBlocked. Crop, resize and extend are also not serialized against each other. Only turn and straighten use _turnQueue, and only turn and straighten set _turning. extendCanvasNow builds `kept` from the layers as they are after the upload (13947) and drops every other layer. generate() does not wait for `_pendingEdits` either, so a run can start in the old geometry while the edit is still uploading.
scenario: (1) 15k document: in the Canvas tool, drag the frame inward and press Enter. The crop then encodes and uploads the new base, which takes over a second at 15k. The window stays live, so the user presses T and starts dragging a layer, or keeps a brush stroke going. The crop commits under the held gesture: l.x -= left and fitView. The next pointermove sets l.x from the drag's old-geometry orig.x with the new view mapping, so the layer lands off by the crop amount. A held stroke draws a streak from p.last (old coordinates) to the next point, into the layer's pixels. (2) Resize (Image panel) pressed and the crop applied inside the same upload window, both from the old W x H. Whichever commits last leaves its base with the other's layer geometry (base at the old scale, layers scaled), and both undo steps hold the pre-state. (3) Extend (left 1024): a stroke made or a layer landed during the multi-second upload is missing from the extended picture, because the flatten was taken before it and the extend then sets `this.layers = kept`; it comes back only by undoing the extend. (4) Generate clicked during that upload with an existing selection on an API recipe: the crop is cut and paid in the old geometry, and the result lands at the old x/y in the extended document, 1024 px off. The same Generate race applies to crop and resize.
fix: Use turnDocumentNow's pattern in crop, resize and extend. Record historyGen, basePx and W/H before the await. After it, abort (release px, the snapshot and the new base, and say in the status line that nothing was changed) when any changed, or when gestureHeld() or turnBlocked() is set. Set _turning during crop, resize and extend, or run them through _turnQueue, so two canvas operations never overlap. Alternatively or as well, have generate() refuse while a tracked geometry edit is pending.
why: Found from two slices. canvas-a verifier: confirmed. cropCanvasNow (5967-6012) checks _turning and turnBlocked once, takes the canvas snapshot, awaits uploadBase (a PNG encode plus upload of the base, a second or more at 15k), then shifts layers, swaps sel and base, runs fitView and pushes the step. It never re-checks. resizeImageNow (6018-6097) and extendCanvasNow (13890-13975, which awaits relightSettled and uploadCanvas after taking its flatten) do the same. turnDocumentNow (5340-5348) does re-check historyGen, basePx, size, gestureHeld and turnBlocked after its upload, with a comment that names this race. None of crop, resize or extend sets _turning or joins _turnQueue, so they can overlap. A stroke or move held over the commit continues under the new fitView mapping (a streak or a jump). A stroke made during extend's upload is left out of the flattened base, and its layer is dropped. Every case is undoable, because the canvas step holds the same px objects. It is still a real race in a window of a second or more. canvas-b verifier: confirmed; `generate()` (24566-24600) checks neither `_pendingEdits` nor `_turning`, and provider results carry no geometry check (only eacharea.js checks `geometrySeq`), so a Generate started during the multi-second upload at 15k cuts and pays for a crop in the old geometry, and the result lands shifted. Effort: canvas-a said medium (the serialization), canvas-b small (the recheck alone).

claim: `restoreSnapshot` and `restoreTurn` apply a whole-document `turn` snapshot that may have another size. They do this without the `turnBlocked()` check and the `_pendingEdits` wait that `historyStepNow` applies to the same `turn` / `canvas` steps (14927: 'a job still running on this document would land where the picture was'). These are the Undo history's snapshot Restore button, MCP `restore_snapshot` and the assistant's Undo this turn.
scenario: Take snapshot 'A' at 3000 x 2000, resize to 6000 x 4000, select a region at (4000, 3000) and start a paid API Generate (or a render on the user's ComfyUI). While it runs, click Restore on 'A' in the history panel. The document becomes 3000 x 2000, and the paid result later lands at (4000, 3000): outside or misplaced. The same happens while an Each area run or an extend's upload is in flight; the extend then overwrites the restored state.
fix: In `restoreTurn`, refuse with `turnBlocked()`'s text when it is non-empty or a gesture is held, and wait for or refuse while `_pendingEdits` is non-empty, as `historyStepNow` does. Have the command, the panel and the assistant report the refusal.
why: Confirmed. `restoreTurn` (14220-14228) and `restoreSnapshot` (14270-14276) apply a whole-document `turn` snapshot, which can have another size, with no `turnBlocked()` check, no `gestureHeld()` check and no wait for `_pendingEdits`. The callers add none either: the history panel's Restore button (inpaint_modal.js:559), MCP `restore_snapshot` (commands.js:2489-2497) and the assistant's Undo this turn (assistant_turns.js:83). `historyStepNow` refuses exactly this for canvas/turn steps (14927-14930). So restoring a snapshot taken at another size during a paid run makes the result land in the wrong geometry.

claim: applyPending (the Apply button / Enter of Rotate, Distort, Warp) never checks the size of the canvas it bakes into. The editor's own makeCanvas (line 836) has no limit check, unlike inpaint_pixels.js makeCanvas, which throws because "a picture of nothing must not be ... baked in". So a transformed box over 268 MP comes back as an empty layer, and the status line reports success. The MCP transform_layer has exactly this guard (commands.js pendingSize, 2147-2154). The UI path never got it, so the two copies have drifted. matchEdges' resample (line 5182) has the same gap for its output canvas.
scenario: A 15000 x 10000 document with a full-size paint or image layer. Transform tool, Rotate, type 30 in Angle (or drag), press Enter. The bake canvas is 17,990 x 16,160 = 291 MP, past Chromium's 268 MP limit, so Chromium draws nothing into it. Layer.fromCanvas reads transparent pixels, and the layer becomes empty at its new box. Any live mask has already been baked in, and the status says "rotate applied (17990 × 16160)". From about 24° up, any rotation of a full 15k x 10k layer does this. So does a distort with one corner dragged far out, and a layer drawn below its own resolution (res > 1), which multiplies the area. Only Ctrl+Z brings it back, and only while the step is still inside the 30-step / 384 MB history.
fix: Move commands.js pendingSize into the editor. In applyPending, compute the size (times res) before pushUndo and applyMask, refuse with canvasSizeRefusal, and have transform_layer call the same check. For bake paths, use inpaint_pixels' makeCanvas, which throws, or check canvasFits, so matchEdges fails loudly too.
why: Confirmed in the snapshot. applyPending (inpaint_canvas.js 3018-3086) pushes the layerfull step and bakes the mask, then calls the editor's local makeCanvas (836-841), which has no limit check, at 3066 for round(bw*res) x round(bh*res). A 30 deg rotation of a full 15000 x 10000 layer gives 17,990 x 16,160 = 290.7 MP. Chromium makes that canvas silently and draws nothing into it (the inpaint_pixels.js:72-73 comment). Layer.fromCanvas then reads it as transparent, and the status says the rotate was applied. commands.js 2147-2154 checks exactly this size for transform_layer, so the UI path and the command have drifted apart. matchEdges (5180-5184) checks the source size but not the output canvas; the fit allows up to 8 % scale, so only a source already near the limit is affected there. Severity lowered from must: on tiles the layerfull step is a copy-on-write clone (snapshot at 14350-14381), so Ctrl+Z gets the pixels and the mask back, and the layer vanishing on screen is visible at once. Nothing is lost silently.

claim: Arrow-key nudging with the Transform tool has two problems. First, it moves the active layer even when it is locked or a filter layer; every other move path refuses those: the pointer path (6411-6412), setLayerGeometry, centerLayer, alignTargets, flipLayer and rotateLayer90. Second, it pushes a separate undo step for every keydown, auto-repeat included, so holding an arrow key evicts the whole history. The Rotate mode's Angle field has the same lock bypass: startPending (2897) and applyPending (3018) never call isLocked, so Rotate + Angle + Apply bakes a locked layer. The MCP command refuses that case.
scenario: (a) Lock a layer, press T, press an arrow key: the locked layer moves. The same happens when several layers are selected and all are locked or filter layers: groupBox() is null and the code falls back to the active layer. (b) With the default 30-step depth, hold ArrowRight for about a second to move a layer 30 px (keyboard repeat is around 30 Hz). That makes 30 "Nudge layer" steps, and every earlier undo step (strokes, a landed result's placement, a crop) is trimmed for good (trimUndo). (c) Lock a layer, click Rotate in the Transform bar, type 15 in Angle, click Apply: the locked layer's pixels are resampled.
fix: Take the nudged layers from alignTargets() (or check isLocked and kind filter), and say so when none is left. Fold a nudge burst into one step: snapshot on the first key, push after about 300 ms without an arrow or before the next other edit. Check isLocked in startPending and again in applyPending.
why: Confirmed. The arrow-key nudge at 3645-3660 checks neither isLocked nor kind filter. groupBox (4172-4179) leaves out locked and filter layers but returns null when nothing is left, and the code then falls back to [l], the active layer, locked or not. The pointer path does refuse locked and filter layers (6414-6416), and so do the other move paths (4952, 5006, 5018). Each keydown, auto-repeat included, calls pushUndo for its own transform step. MAX_UNDO is 30 (line 81), so holding an arrow for about a second trims every earlier step (trimUndo 14418-14424). The relight nudge just below folds a burst into one step. startPending (2897-2915), the Angle input (2508) and applyPending (3018) never call isLocked. So Rotate, an angle typed in, then Apply bakes a locked layer's pixels. The command path refuses that case through refuseLayer.

claim: ask() puts a window-wide capture keydown listener on the page that takes Enter and Escape and never checks host.isActive(this). Inactive tabs stay open and are only hidden (host.activate toggles shell-hidden), and closeDocument and Ctrl+Tab do not look at askOpen. So a question left open in a background tab answers itself from keys typed in another tab, and it swallows those keys. close() does not finish an open question either: its listener and its closure, which holds the whole closed document, stay alive until the next Enter or Escape. That key then resolves the dead editor's promise, and its caller continues on a closed document.
scenario: Tab A: open "Clear the history" (danger confirm, 21381), or Resize / Import SVG. Without answering, press Ctrl+Tab (Next Tab) to tab B, click into B's prompt field and press Enter or Ctrl+Enter. B's _docKey returns early for a field, and A's onKey then does preventDefault + stopImmediatePropagation and finish(answer()). A's results history is cleared, or A resizes with the prefilled size, in the background. B's Ctrl+Enter generate never fires. If B was opened after A's question, A's listener runs first and takes every Enter and Escape in B, even outside fields.
fix: In onKey, return unless host.isActive(this) and the event's target is inside wrap, or document.activeElement is. In close(), finish the open question with null (keep a reference to its finish), so the listener goes and the caller sees a cancel. Optionally, finish or block the question when its tab is deactivated.
why: Confirmed. ask() (3309-3488) registers a capture keydown listener on window (3478). On Enter and Escape it calls preventDefault, stopImmediatePropagation and finish, and never checks host.isActive(this) or where the event came from. Inactive tabs are only hidden (host.js 802/842, shell-hidden is display:none). The overlay sits inside the editor root, so the tab bar is still usable, and CmdOrCtrl+Tab is a menu accelerator (main.js:703) that onKey does not catch. In tab B, B's _docKey returns early for a field (3161), so A's listener takes an Enter typed in any field of B. That answers A's question: clearHistory (21376-21385) then clears A's results history, which no undo step brings back.
