If B was opened after A asked, A's listener runs first for every Enter and Escape in B. close() (3191ff.) removes _docKey and _docKeyUp but leaves an open question's listener and its closure, which holds the closed document. The shell's own key handlers do check ed.askOpen (shell.js 3028, 3160), but only for the active editor.

claim: On tiles, the SAM2 selection clipped to the active layer (Object source "active layer", or an object map made on a layer) builds its clip with storeArgs(layer.px, layer.x, layer.y). That store is read 1:1 at (x|0, y|0) with the pixels' own size (inpaint_worker.js storeRows). It ignores the layer's displayed size, a fractional position and the layer's live mask. The canvas-backend twin (layerAlpha, 12637) draws the layer at x, y, w, h through layerPixels, mask included. So the two backends give different selections, and the tile one is wrong for any scaled or masked layer.
scenario: Resize image to 50 %: every layer keeps its own resolution, so px is twice w x h. Then, with Object source = active layer on a cut-out layer, click the object. The clip is the cut-out's alpha at twice its shown size, anchored at its top left. The selection keeps pixels outside the object's real silhouette and drops parts inside it. A layer with a mask hiding half of it is selected through the hidden half. A Generate on that selection inpaints the wrong region, which costs money on an API recipe.
fix: Pass storeArgs only when px.width === l.w, px.height === l.h, x and y are whole and there is no live mask. Otherwise send the clip band as bytes drawn at the layer's box through its mask, as layerAlpha does, or give storeRows a scale and a mask store, as the stack entries already have.
why: Confirmed. On tiles with the pool on, selectLogits (7995) builds the clip with storeArgs(layer.px, layer.x, layer.y, ...) (inpaint_bands.js 141-149: w and h are snap.width and snap.height). The worker reads it with storeRows (inpaint_worker.js 230-254): 1:1 at (x|0, y|0), at the pixels' own size, alpha only, no mask (1300-1303, 1350). The layer's displayed w x h, a fractional position and its live mask are all ignored. The canvas path, layerAlpha (12637ff.), draws layerPixels (mask applied) at layer.x, y, w, h. Scaled layers are common: Transform-handle scaling changes only w and h, and Resize keeps every layer's own resolution. host.selectBox and selectPoint (host.js 6627-6671) pass the active layer when Object source is 'active layer' or the object map is a layer's. So the tile backend's selection is clipped by a silhouette of the wrong size, and a masked layer is selected through its hidden part. The marching ants show the wrong selection before any run, so money is only spent if the user does not notice.

claim: A new picture loaded into the same tab keeps the old picture's document state. This covers loadFile (Ctrl+drop, paste into an empty tab, the node's open), setBaseFromRef and MCP `load_image` (path or filename), loadTiff and loadLayered. setBasePixels(keepLayers:false) resets layers, undo and snapshots, but not `maps` (the depth map), `history` (results), `savedSelections`, `guides`, `compare` or `_solo`. newCanvas and setBaseFromCanvas reset most of these by hand (21333-21341), so the two copies of the rule have drifted.
scenario: Tab with photo A and its computed depth map. Ctrl+drop photo B onto the canvas, or an agent calls load_image (whose description says it replaces image, layers and history). Adding Lens blur, Depth fog, a depth Limit or Relight renders B with A's depth. If B has another size, A's map is also placed by its old xf. The map is saved into B's document. The Results panel lists A's results as '(discarded)' with Restore, and Restore pastes A's patch onto B. A solo left over from before (`_solo`) means the next Alt+click's 'restore' does nothing (its `known` ids are A's).
fix: In setBasePixels when !keepLayers, reset history, savedSelections, maps (mapsVersion++), guides, compare and _solo. Remove the duplicated resets from newCanvas and setBaseFromCanvas.
why: Confirmed. setBasePixels (18461-18511) with keepLayers:false clears layers, undo and snapshots, but not maps/mapsVersion, history, savedSelections, guides, compare or _solo. newCanvas (21337-21341) and setBaseFromCanvas (21133-21139) reset these by hand, so the two copies of the rule have drifted. loadFile (Ctrl+drop at 2334/3284, paste, shell.js:320/3404), setBaseFromRef (18403-18424) and load_image all go through setBasePixels. load_image clears only history itself (commands.js:1163). The new picture keeps the old depth map: add_filter/relight check only that a map exists (commands.js:2356-2359, inpaint_canvas.js:15361-15363), and the fp check runs only inside computeDepthMap (13080), so lens blur, depth fog, relight and depth limits render B with A's depth. The Depth row only says '(stale)'. A's results stay in the Results panel, and Restore pastes them onto B.

claim: getValue writes `match` only when strength > 0, and setValue falls back to source 'surroundings' (24893). A layer whose match source is 'underneath' at strength 0 loses that source on every save and autosave restore. The Realism Pass layer (host.js:3945, documented as 'its source is underneath'), the key layer (host.js:4699) and the generative-relight pixel layer (host.js:5344) are all made that way.
scenario: Run the Realism Pass. The whole-picture layer comes with match strength 0, source underneath. Save the .scumble (or restart the app) and reopen it, then drag the layer's Match slider to 60: nothing changes. With source 'surroundings' the ring of a full-frame layer lies outside the canvas, statsOfMatch finds fewer than 64 backdrop pixels and returns null. Before the save the same drag worked.
fix: Write `match` whenever it differs from the default, i.e. `l.match && (l.match.strength > 0 || l.match.source === "underneath")`.
why: Confirmed. getValue writes match only when `l.match.strength > 0` (24701), and setValue falls back to {strength 0, source surroundings} (24893). The Realism Pass layer (host.js:3945), the key layer (host.js:4700) and the generative-relight pixel layer (host.js:5343) are all created with {strength 0, source underneath}. After a save and reopen (or an autosave restore) the source is 'surroundings'. For an opaque whole-frame layer, statsOfMatch (22587-22610) counts ring pixels only where the layer alpha is 127 or less, so ns=0, it returns null, and the Match slider does nothing. The user can switch back in the source select (19148), but nothing says the source was lost.

claim: mergeInto draws the lower layer's raw pixels (17314, layerPixels has no colour match) and then sets `below.match` to strength 0. The lower layer's own colour match is thrown away without a word. The status line warns only about the upper layer's match (17269), and mergeSelected's `unbaked` check skips sel[0], the survivor (17286). Merge into the base, by contrast, does bake the match (drawLayer on a full canvas).
scenario: Result 2 has Match 80 and Result 3 sits above it with no match. Ctrl+E on Result 3: Result 2's area jumps back to its unmatched colours. The status reads 'Result 3 merged into Result 2.' as info. The user notices later; only Ctrl+Z brings the match back.
fix: When matchActive(below), draw its matched pixels into the merge canvas (as drawLayer does for the base merge). At least include the lower layer in the 'not baked' warning in both mergeDown and mergeSelected.
why: Confirmed. mergeInto draws `this.layerPixels(below)` (17313), which applies the mask and the stroke but no colour match, then sets `below.match = { strength: 0, source: 'surroundings' }` (17361). mergeDown's status warns only about the upper layer's match (17269), and mergeSelected's `unbaked` uses sel.slice(1), skipping the survivor (17286). A lower result layer with Match > 0 visibly jumps back to its unmatched colours under an 'info' status. Ctrl+Z restores it, and the change is visible, so should rather than must.

claim: soloResult, which runs on a plain click on a history thumbnail and on the row's solo button, changes the visibility of every layer with kind 'result', reference and control layers included. setLayerRole keeps kind 'result' when a result is turned into a reference. It also records nothing to restore: no `_solo` and no undo step. The layer solo (soloLayers) leaves references alone, as the manual says.
scenario: A result was turned into a reference and is used as @img1. The user clicks another result's thumbnail in the history to look at it. The reference is hidden and its @img1 token parks as @img?, so the next Generate refuses or goes without that picture. A result used as a depth control is hidden too. No Alt+click or 'Show all layers' brings the earlier visibility back; each eye has to be clicked by hand.
fix: Restrict it to `l.kind === "result" && !this.isReference(l) && !this.isControl(l)`, and record the previous visibility (as soloLayers does in _solo) so the same click or 'Show all layers' restores it.
why: Confirmed. soloResult (21100-21114) sets `l.visible = l.id === h.layerId` for every layer with kind 'result', whatever its role. setLayerRole (4442-4457) changes only role, so a result turned into a reference or a control keeps kind 'result' and is hidden by a plain thumbnail click (20971) or the row's solo button (20997). refsMutated then parks its @img token. soloResult also keeps no `_solo` record, unlike soloLayers (17139-17154, which skips references), so neither Alt+click nor 'Show all layers' brings the visibility back. The next Generate goes without that picture or is refused, which can waste a paid API run.

claim: segmentKey reuses editor.objects.hash as the SAM2 embedding key whenever the object map covers the same source and size. It never compares the map's version with editor.compositeVersion. After any change to the picture, a point or box segmentation therefore decodes on main's cached embedding of the old picture: main's segment() finds the old key in Sam2.cache. A map read from a layer is never treated as stale anywhere, because updateObjectHover only checks staleness when layerId === null (inpaint_canvas.js:12943), so its hover map and its clicks stay on the old pixels too.
scenario: With the Object tool, the user hovers once, so findObjects caches the embedding under 'node:image:H1' and sets objects.version = v1. A Generate result then lands (or the user paints, or presses Ctrl+Z), giving v2. Next, the assistant or an MCP agent calls select_point (commands.js:1267 -> segmentLogits). Or the user drags an object box without moving the mouse in between, so no hover refresh runs. segmentKey answers the old key, main decodes on the embedding of the picture before the edit, and the new selection outlines what used to be there. A following inpaint then repaints the wrong area.
fix: In segmentKey, reuse o.hash only when o.version === editor.compositeVersion for a whole-picture map. For a layer map, also record and compare the layer's pixel version. Otherwise fall through to the _segmentKeyCache path, which already keys on compositeVersion. In updateObjectHover and toggleObjectAt, treat a stale map (either kind) as missing: ensureObjects first, or for an in-app click go to host.selectPoint rather than drawing the old shape.
why: Confirmed. In renderer/editor/host.js:6580-6585, segmentKey returns `${node.id}:${o.hash}` whenever editor.objects matches the source and size, with no version check. editor.objects is cleared only in the constructor and in dropCompositeCaches (inpaint_canvas.js:5568, flips and half turns). A Generate result, paint or undo bumps compositeVersion and leaves the old map and hash in place. On the main side, onnx/index.js:227-230 segment() takes sam.cache.get(req.key), and sam2.js keeps the last 3 embeddings (54-70). So the old embedding is found and decoded, and the selection follows the picture before the edit. commands.js select_point (1267) calls host.segmentLogits directly and never goes through the hover refresh, so an MCP or assistant select_point after a generate segments the old picture. selectBox (6638) and selectPoint (6663) do the same when no hover refresh ran in between. If the old embedding was evicted, the retry re-encodes the new picture under the old key, which is harmless but mislabelled. Layer maps are never treated as stale: updateObjectHover (12941-12943) tests staleness only when layerId === null, and toggleObjectAt (12957-12961) uses the map's shape with no staleness check at all. Neither verified.json nor BUGS.md Open has it, and U1 moves the ONNX sessions without touching this renderer key logic.

claim: Once the tile atlas reaches its budget mid-frame, `composite()` returns null at line 1044. That is before `_evictAtlas()` (line 1209), the only place pages from earlier frames are dropped. So the atlas never gets back under budget, and every later frame at that view fails the same way. The GPU compositor stays off until the view returns to a level where every store already has slots, or until releaseCaches clears the atlas.
scenario: 4K monitor, a 15000 x 10000 document with base + 3 full paint layers (the perf doc). At fit (level 2) each store holds about 41 MB of pages, 165 MB in all. Zoom to about 30% (level 1, about 1,700 visible tiles, about 113 MB of pages per store). In that frame the fit pages still count. `_slot` (649-684) may only make a new page while `atlasBytes < atlasBudget`. The 4th store crosses 512 MB with no free slot left in its pages, so it returns null, `_tileInstances` returns null (743/751), and so does `composite`. The next frame starts at about 516 MB again and fails at the same store. Every frame now walks and uploads slots, gives up, and then draws through the Canvas 2D region path. On a QHD screen the same happens with base + 5 full layers, or fewer layers that carry full masks. No test runs the compositor over its budget.
fix: In `composite`, when `_tileInstances` returns null, call `this._evictAtlas()` (it already skips pages used this frame) and retry that layer once before returning null. At the least, call it before the `return null`, so the next frame finds the stale pages gone. Alternatively, in `_slot`, before giving up, drop the least recently used pages of other entries that were not used this frame. Add a composite gate step: `setAtlasBudget` small (e.g. 64 MB), a plain stack of 2-3 whole-picture tile layers, fit, then zoom into the next level. Assert that `composite` returned a canvas (the GPU path ran) and that `stats().atlas.bytes` is back under the budget.
why:
The code shows it. In `_slot` (inpaint_compositor.js:649-684) a new page is made only while `atlasBytes < atlasBudget`. Past the budget, the only fallback reuses a slot of the same entry that was not used this frame. A level the view has just entered is a new entry, so all its slots are used this frame, `_slot` returns null, `_tileInstances` returns null (743/751), and `composite` returns null at 1044. `_evictAtlas()`, the only place that ages out or LRU-drops the old level's pages, runs only at 1209 on the success path. `retainPixels` keeps live pixels' records and does not trim their old levels. A null from `glViewComposite` does not latch `compositorOff`. So every later frame at that zoom band retries and fails at the same store.

The numbers hold. The canvas is in device pixels (resizeCanvas, dpr). Level = floor(-log2(scale)), so fit is level 2. Level-2 pages are 4.46 MB (256 slots), about 45 MB per 15k store. Level-1 pages are 17.3 MB (256 slots). At scale 0.26 on a 4K view, each store needs about 1,500 tiles, so 4 stores need about 416 MB on top of 178 MB of stale fit pages, more than 512 MB.

It is not permanent. It recovers once the view reaches a zoom where the failing store's own existing slots cover the view (deeper in, at about 0.45). Or it recovers at fit, where every level-2 entry is full and a success runs the eviction. The scenario's '(the perf doc)' is wrong: perf_test's stack carries a filter layer, so `glCompositeUsable` keeps it on Canvas 2D. The defect holds for a plain stack of base + 3 whole-picture layers (duplicates, a Realism Pass, a relight or a key layer; full masks count as stores too). It is not in verified.json or BUGS.md Open, and no gate composites over the budget.

claim: `setAtlasBudget(bytes)` does `Math.max(16 MB, bytes | 0)`. The shell passes `atlasMB * 1048576` (renderer/shell.js:149-152, inpaint_canvas.js:21683), and the Settings field has no maximum (renderer/index.html:173). Any value of 2048 MB or more overflows the 32-bit OR to a negative number or 0, and the budget becomes 16 MB. A large value can also wrap to an arbitrary one: 5000 MB gives 904 MB.
scenario: A user with a 32 GB card raises Settings › Rendering › Tile atlas to 2048 or 4096 MB to get rid of stutter. The budget silently drops to 16 MB. At fit on a 15k document, the base store alone needs about 41 MB of level-2 pages. After 4 pages (17.8 MB) no new page is allowed, `_slot` returns null, and per T1 the GPU compositor never composites that document. Every frame falls back to Canvas 2D: the opposite of what the user asked for.
fix: `this.atlasBudget = Math.max(16 * 1048576, Math.floor(Number(bytes)) || 0);` with no bitwise operator. Optionally give the Settings field and `applyAtlasBudget` a sane maximum (e.g. 16384 MB) and clamp there.
why:
Confirmed at inpaint_compositor.js:582-583: `Math.max(16 * 1024 * 1024, bytes | 0)`. Both callers pass `atlasMB * 1048576`: shell.js:152 and inpaint_canvas.js:21683, where it is applied at start from the stored setting too. The `set-atlas` input (index.html:173) has min 16 and no max. shell.js:2814 and wholeMB clamp only from below.

The wrap: 2048 MB is 2^31, which `| 0` turns into -2^31. 3072 MB gives a negative number, 4096 MB gives 0, and 6144 MB gives -2^31, so each becomes the 16 MB floor. 5000 MB wraps to 947,912,704 bytes (904 MB).

At 16 MB, a 15k base store at fit needs about 45 MB of level-2 pages. After four 4.46 MB pages (17.8 MB) no new page is allowed and no slot can be reused in the first frame, so `composite` returns null on every frame. A second store fails even at 1:1. A user who raises the budget for a large card silently gets the Canvas 2D path everywhere. The only test (editor_test.py) uses 464 MB.

claim: After a WebGL context loss, an editor's GPU compositor never comes back. `compositor()` caches `this._compositor` (21677-21690). The compositor's `webglcontextlost` handler only sets `lost = true` (inpaint_compositor.js:410). There is no `webglcontextrestored` handling and no rebuild, so `composite()` returns null at line 1027 for the rest of the document's life. The filter GL module does handle this: inpaint_filters_gl.js:672-679 makes a new context when the old one is lost. In the same way, any one exception inside a frame sets `compositorOff = true` for good (21787).
scenario: A GPU process reset (a TDR under VRAM pressure while ComfyUI holds the card, or a driver update). Or more than about 15 open documents: each editor has its own WebGL2 context, and Chromium loses the oldest one past 16 per page. Every affected document then renders through the Canvas 2D path until it is closed and reopened or the app restarts; filters come back, compositing does not. The same happens after one RangeError while allocating a chain or edge buffer near the 15.5 GB typed-array limit inside `_tileInstances`. At 15k the pan and stroke frames are then the slow path for the rest of the session.
fix: In `compositor()`: if `this._compositor && this._compositor.lost && !this._destroyed`, dispose it and set `this._compositor = undefined` so a fresh `GLCompositor` is built (its atlas and textures start empty anyway). Better, rebuild on the canvas's `webglcontextrestored`, or only for the front editor, so tabs do not evict each other's contexts in a ping-pong past 16. Let `compositorOff` expire, for example retry on the next document change or after N frames. Test: `getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext()`, then `restoreContext()` on the compositor's context, then assert that `glViewComposite` returns a canvas again.
why:
Confirmed. `compositor()` (inpaint_canvas.js:21676-21690) returns the cached `this._compositor` whenever it is not undefined. The only reset is `destroy()` (25304). The compositor's `webglcontextlost` handler (inpaint_compositor.js:410) calls preventDefault and sets `lost = true`. Nothing listens for `webglcontextrestored` or rebuilds the GL objects, and `composite` returns null at 1027 while `lost`. So after a GPU-process reset or driver TDR, or after Chromium drops the oldest of more than 16 contexts, that editor draws through Canvas 2D until the tab is closed. At 15k that means thousands of putImageData tiles per frame at fit.

The filter module does rebuild its context (inpaint_filters_gl.js:672-679). The memory watch's `clear()` and `releaseGpu` (the filter pool) do not touch `lost`. Any exception in `glViewComposite` latches `compositorOff = true` with no reset (21787). That is a stated design choice ('also what happens after a failure'), but it has the same permanent effect.

GPU pressure from ComfyUI on the same card is a realistic trigger. PHASE6_PLAN H6 notes the 16-context limit but not the missing recovery, and neither verified.json nor BUGS.md Open lists it. Context loss is rare, which is why this is should and not must.

claim: A close, View > Reload and the update install all wait for .scumble saves (host.docSavesIdle, and documents.idle in main's flushAll at main.js:481) but not for an export. flushAll never looks at fileSaves, and the window's app:flush handler does not know an export is running.
scenario: The user exports a 15k PSD or TIFF, which takes several seconds of packing in the workers and then goes to main in 64 MB pieces. While the status line says 'Saving ... 40 %', the user closes the window. saveBeforeRestart returns almost at once because the layers were already saved, and main closes the window. The remaining pieces never arrive, and will-quit drops the save and deletes its temp (main.js:1407-1411). The target stays as it was, and no question, status line or log entry says the export never happened.
fix: Track exports in flight in the host (a set that exportImage, exportLayerPng and exportMaskPng enter and leave around saveExport), and await it in the onFlush handler before saveBeforeRestart. Also let flushAll wait for !fileSaves.busy, bounded by QuitGuard's timeout, so that 'Keep waiting / Quit now' covers exports too.
why: Confirmed. The window's app:flush handler (shell.js:2876-2882) waits only for host.docSavesIdle (.scumble saves in _docSaves, host.js:5900-5907) and saveBeforeRestart. saveExport (host.js:5810-5830) is not tracked anywhere. Main's flushAll (main.js:481-485) awaits flushWindow and documents.idle(), never fileSaves. The close handler (main.js:381-386) then closes the window, and will-quit (main.js:1407-1412) calls fileSaves.abortAll(), which deletes the temp. The target stays as it was and no log line or question appears. Closing right after clicking Export is a natural sequence, and a 15k PSD or TIFF export takes seconds, so the export is lost without a word.

claim: resolveLayer gives every non-read document call the active layer's id as `layer` when the model left it out (relight is the only exception). Three commands refuse an unexpected layer: select_color with sample image throws 'layer goes with sample layer' (commands.js:1299), set_crop throws 'unknown crop setting "layer"' (commands.js:1450-1452), and boxes_add / boxes_set resolve `layer` as a reference layer before they look at the kind (boxes_model.js:78). On any document with an active layer, these tools can never run from the assistant.
scenario: A document with one result layer. The user asks for the sky with the magic wand, and the model calls select_color {x, y}: the call goes out as {x, y, layer: '<result id>'} and fails. A retry with layer 'active' is turned into the same id, so the call fails twice and is refused. set_crop {fill: 'green'} fails the same way, and boxes_add {kind: 'new', rect} fails with '<name> is not a reference layer'. When the active layer is a reference, a from box without layer silently takes it. The only tests are policy-decision rows, which never run the canonical call.
fix: Fill layer only when the tool's schema has a layer property that is its target. Skip set_crop and other tools without one. Skip select_color unless sample is 'layer', and boxes_add / boxes_set unless kind is 'from'. Add a test that runs resolveLayer's output through these command handlers.
why: Confirmed. resolveLayer (electron/main/assistant/index.js:1012-1015) gives every non-read call that takes doc or a layer (wantsLayers, :718-737) the active layer's id when layer is missing. The MCP server passes arguments through unvalidated (mcp/server.js:118-121), and commands.run does too (commands.js:3116-3122). Three commands then fail. select_color with sample image throws 'layer goes with sample layer' for any id other than 'active' (commands.js:1299). set_crop loops over every key and throws 'unknown crop setting "layer"' (commands.js:1450-1452); set_crop is document-scoped, so it gets doc and wantsLayers is true. normaliseBox calls referenceId(a.layer) before it looks at kind (boxes_model.js:78), so boxes_add / boxes_set fail on a non-reference active layer, and a 'from' box silently takes an active reference. The assistant tests only check policy decisions for these calls (assistant_test.js:1275, 1289, 1296), never the canonical args sent to the command.

claim: `snapshotLayer` copies the whole layer with `{ ...l }`, and every `layers` / `canvas` undo step stores those copies. The copies keep the layer's full-size cache canvases (`_masked`, `_fcache`, `_mcache*`, `_fxCache*`). So `releaseCaches` (24458-24470, the memory watch and background tabs) clears these fields on the live layers only, and the undo stack keeps every canvas alive. `turnSnapshot` already sets exactly these fields to null for this reason (14191, 'would only keep what the document replaces later alive'); the rule was never brought to `snapshotLayer`.
scenario: 15000 x 10000 document with a full-size masked paint layer and a filter layer. Ctrl+C on the masked layer builds `_masked` (600 MB). A copy merged or an extend builds the filter's `_fcache` (600 MB). Then add, reorder or set_layer a few times (each pushes a `layers` step). Switch tabs: the memory watch's `releaseCaches` reports about 1.2 GB freed, but every undo record still holds both canvases, so GPU / renderer memory does not go down. A resize or extend (a `canvas` step) then makes new caches at the new size beside the retained old ones, which doubles that memory until the step is trimmed.
fix: Use one helper that drops every derived cache field (`_masked`, `_maskedValid`, `_fcache`, `_fcacheView`, `_fcacheSample`, `_mcache`, `_mcacheView`, `_mcacheSample`, `_fxCache`, `_fxCacheView`, `_fxCacheSample`, `_mstats*`, `_bstats*`, `_relight`) from the record. Call it in both `snapshotLayer` and `turnSnapshot`. `applySnapshot` rebuilds them on demand.
why: Confirmed in the code. `snapshotLayer` (inpaint_canvas.js:14151-14166) returns `{ ...l }` and deletes only LAYER_PENDING_KEYS, so every `layers` step (14344) and `canvas` step (14361) keeps the layer's `_masked`, `_fcache*`, `_mcache*`, `_fxCache*` and `_relight` objects. `releaseCaches` (24454-24480) nulls these fields only on `this.layers`. `filteredCanvas` makes a new canvas and slot object on every recompute (15645), and a layers step bumps compositeVersion, so each of the up to MAX_UNDO=30 steps pins its own view or full-size cache canvas per filter or matched layer, outside the undo byte budget. The memory census already counts undo-held `_masked` (25263), so the retention is visible but never fixed. `turnSnapshot` (14191) nulls only `_masked`, `_mcache`, `_fcache` and `_fxCache`, and misses the View/Sample slots too.

claim: `copySelection({ merged })` (Ctrl+Shift+C, `copy_to_layer` merged, and Ctrl+C with a filter layer active) calls `flattenToCanvas()` for the whole document to copy a selection of any size. With filter layers, `drawComposite` also builds and keeps the 600 MB `flatCanvas`. `flattenToCanvas` throws for documents above 268 MP. The non-merged branch copies the whole layer through `layerPixels(layer)` -> `toCanvas()`. `readBoxBytes` / `readBox(box)` already composite exactly a box over the tiles.
scenario: 15000 x 10000 document with a film look and a levels layer. Select 500 x 500 px and press Ctrl+Shift+C: the window blocks for the whole full-resolution composite (seconds with the film look) and keeps a 600 MB canvas. On a 30000 x 20000 document the copy throws 'larger than any canvas' and nothing is copied.
fix: For a selection, read only its bounds: `readBoxBytes([x0, y0, x1, y1], { forRun: true })` or `readBox` for merged, and the layer's box for the layer copy (this makes the copy async). Keep the whole flatten for `copyLayer`.
why: Confirmed. In `copySelection` (12361-12383), `useMerged` is true for Ctrl+Shift+C, with a filter layer active, and with no active layer (the base: the common case of selecting on the picture and pressing Ctrl+C). It then calls `flattenToCanvas({ forRun: true })`, which builds a full-resolution canvas of the document and composites it synchronously (22704-22716). It copies out only w x h. At 15000 x 10000 that is a 600 MB canvas, and BUGS.md measures a whole flatten at 3.4 s (8.2 s with a film look) for a copy of any size. Above 268 MP `flattenToCanvas` throws (huge). The non-merged branch also materialises the whole layer through `layerPixels(layer)`. `readBoxBytes` (9101) and `readBox` (9274) already composite a box.

claim: `saveSelection` stores `this.sel.toCanvas().toDataURL("image/png")`: a full-document canvas and a synchronous PNG encode on the main thread. `encodeSelectionSoon` was rewritten for this exact reason ('It was sel.toCanvas(): a canvas of the whole image for every change ... 600 MB at 15000 x 10000, and nothing at all above the canvas limit'), but the saved-selection path still does it.
scenario: 15000 x 10000 document with a small marquee, click Save selection: a 600 MB canvas is made and encoded synchronously, which freezes the window for seconds. Above 268 MP `toCanvas()` throws in the click handler and nothing is saved or said. The resulting data URL is put into every autosave and every .scumble save.
fix: Encode only the selection's bounds off the main thread (`sel.readRect` of `sel.bounds()` plus `canvasToBlob`, as `encodeSelectionSoon` does). Store `{ url, box }`, and have `loadSelection` draw the image at the box's origin, keeping its orient/xf handling.
why: Confirmed. `saveSelection` (9336-9345) stores `this.sel.toCanvas().toDataURL("image/png")`: on tiles a full-document canvas is materialised (600 MB at 15k) and encoded to PNG synchronously in the click handler. `encodeSelectionSoon` (24624-24650) was rewritten to avoid exactly this; its comment quotes the 600 MB problem. Above 268 MP `toCanvas()` throws and nothing is saved. Not in BUGS.md or the external review.

claim: maskToCanvas builds the whole-picture mask on the window: a readRect of the full selection, a full-size ImageData, a JS loop over every pixel, a full-size canvas, then a single-worker PNG encode (encodeCanvas). serializeForPrompt does this for every local ComfyUI run after any selection change (25047), and exportMaskPng does it too. The selection's own save already avoids this whole-image path (encodeSelectionSoon's note).
scenario: 15,000 x 10,000 document, local recipe. After each new selection, Generate copies 600 MB (readRect), allocates another 600 MB (ImageData), runs a 150-million-iteration loop and a 600 MB putImageData (about 2.4 GB transient, counting the canvas). The window is blocked for roughly a second or more (inferred, not measured), followed by a multi-second single-worker deflate. The composite of the same run already goes out in pooled bands.
fix: Encode the grey mask from the selection's tiles in pool parts (the encodeTilePixels / encodeComposite band path, alpha copied to grey per band), with no full-size ImageData or canvas on the window. Use it for exportMaskPng too.
why: Confirmed. maskToCanvas (22864-22876) does a full-size `sel.readRect` (600 MB RGBA at 15000x10000), `createImageData` (another 600 MB), a JS loop over 150M pixels and a full putImageData on the window. uploadCanvas then does createImageBitmap plus a single worker PNG encode (inpaint_encode.js:23-29). serializeForPrompt calls it for every local ComfyUI run whenever maskHash is reset, i.e. after each selection change (25046-25050). exportMaskPng uses it too (18024). The composite of the same run already goes out in pooled bands. Nothing in BUGS.md, PERFORMANCE.md or the wasm plan covers this window path (the plan's maskToCanvas is stitch.js's). The size of the block is inferred, not measured.

claim: `TileMaskPixels.combine` makes every existing tile in the source's box writable and rewrites it, even when the combine cannot change it. Cases: add or subtract with a SEL_NONE view, or intersect with SEL_FULL. Both kernel routes call `write()`: the twin always calls it first (kernels.js:559), and Rust calls it for any non-empty result (px.js:537-541). Since the undo snapshot shares the selection's tiles (snapshotSelection, copyRect over whole tiles), each such tile is copied (256 KB). Its version moves, so its mip chain, atlas slots and region cells are thrown away. The undo step keeps the original alongside the copy.
scenario: 15000 x 10000 picture with a selection covering half of it (about 1,180 tiles). Select by depth with Shift (add) or Shift+Alt (intersect: bandMode 'subtract' with an inverted source, inpaint_canvas.js:7369). `rangeSelectJob` leaves out all-zero tiles (inpaint_worker.js:1192), so every existing selection tile outside the new range (inside it, for intersect) gets SEL_NONE. Each of those is copied and run through the kernel unchanged: about 300 MB of copies plus new arena slots, about 1,000 chains rebuilt in the mips worker while the screen shows stale cells, and the selection's memory doubled for as long as the undo step lives. The same happens for add with a wand or SAM tile source whose box spans existing selection tiles.
fix: In `combine`, before `selCombine`: `if (had && ((v.kind === SEL_NONE && (m === 1 || m === 2)) || (v.kind === SEL_FULL && m === 3))) continue;`. The tile keeps its bytes, version and extent. That is byte-exact where the tile is canonical (the selection colour where alpha > 0, zeros elsewhere), which the combine, fill and invert writers keep. Confirm with the pixels gate on both routes. Optionally also skip the wasted copy in the twins' route for SEL_FULL under subtract (it copies, then drops the tile). Add a pixels_test case: an add of a SEL_NONE view over an existing frozen tile leaves the same tile object, version and `frozen` count.
why:
Confirmed. In `TileMaskPixels.combine` (inpaint_tiles.js:2601-2636) an existing tile is skipped only for `!had && SEL_NONE`. Anything else goes to `selCombine`. The twins' route calls `write()` (`this.writable`) before the combine for every existing tile (kernels.js:555-559). The Rust route calls it for every non-empty result (px.js:537-541), and an unchanged non-empty tile is non-empty.

`writable` (967-997) copies a frozen tile (256 KB) or bumps its version, and calls `_changed`. `snapshotSelection` (14053-14067) takes `copyRect` over whole tiles, and `_copyTileBlock` (1586-1592) shares them, so right after the undo snapshot every selection tile is frozen.

In `selectRange` (7362-7520), add mode passes each band's result through `tilesSource(res.tiles, [0,0], [0, y0, W, y1])`. Its `view` answers VIEW_NONE for every tile the job left out (inpaint_raster.js:481-482). So every existing selection tile in a band with any new tile is copied, run through the kernel unchanged, given a new version (its chain is rebuilt in the worker) and kept alongside the original the step now holds alone. Intersect (bandMode subtract, inverted source) does the same to the tiles inside the range.

With half of a 15k picture selected, that is up to about 1,180 tiles: about 300 MB of copies, the kernel's in and out copies for each, and the step's memory charged against the history budget, which can push older undo steps out. It is not covered by verified.json, BUGS.md or K5's notes.

claim: The depth map's `static: true` sampler never hits the texture cache. rg8View(map) builds a new Uint8Array view of map.data on every call, and uploadSampler keys staticTextures by the identity of `v.data` (inpaint_filters_gl.js:1051-1061). So every values() call of relight (:2085), haze (:266), dehaze (:473), lens blur (inpaint_lensblur.js:439) and the depth limit stage (inpaint_limit.js:80) runs gl.createTexture and a full texImage2D of the map. The guide, normals and shadow-map samplers are cached correctly because they pass stable arrays.
scenario: Take a 15000 x 10000 picture whose depth map is at WORK_MAX, 4096 x 2731 (22.4 MB as RG8), with a relight layer and a lens blur layer above it. Every frame of a light drag re-renders both filters: two new textures and two 22.4 MB uploads on the window thread, a third with a depth-limited fill or filter layer. Every pan frame does the same, since the filter key holds the view. The old textures are released only when the garbage collector finalizes their wrappers, so VRAM grows by about 45-67 MB per frame during the drag. film_test.py's 'a static value uploads once' check passes only because it reuses one data object.
fix: Hand out one stable view per map data. Memoize it in a WeakMap keyed by map.data, or store it on the map object; rebuilding the map changes map.data, and the key already carries dataVersion. Alternatively, key staticTextures by the underlying typed array map.data instead of the view. Extend film_test's static case to call rg8View twice on the same map and expect g.uploads to rise only once.
why: The code shows it. rg8View (inpaint_maps.js:212-221) returns `data: new Uint8Array(map.data.buffer, ...)`, which is a new view object on every call. uploadSampler caches static samplers in a WeakMap keyed by that `v.data` object (inpaint_filters_gl.js:637, :1050-1062), so every call misses: a gl.createTexture plus a texImage2D of the whole RG8 map (4096 x 2731 x 2 = 22.4 MB at WORK_MAX 4096). applyPluginGL calls def.values() on every apply (:1127) and uploads every sampler (:1137-1141). values() calls rg8View on each run of relight (inpaint_relight.js:2085), haze (inpaint_depthfx.js:266), dehaze (:473), lens blur (inpaint_lensblur.js:439) and the depth limit (inpaint_limit.js:80). guideView passes the stable map.guide and is cached correctly. A filter re-runs on every pan frame (vp is in filterKey) and on every param or light change, so a 15k document with depth filters pays one 22 MB upload per depth filter per frame on the window thread. It pays them again for every band of a tiled export (bandFilter per band). The orphaned textures are freed only when the GC collects their wrappers. film_test's static check reuses a single data object (film_test.py:271), so it cannot catch this. Neither verified.json nor BUGS.md covers it. It is a felt slowdown, not wrong pixels, so should is right.

claim: restore() treats every setValue that leaves no picture as 'files not in the local store, wait for ComfyUI' (`_pendingStates` and `_rawStates`), and the parked tab looks like an empty 'Untitled' tab with nothing to save. (a) documentDirty (5959) and rememberClosed (6154) return early on `!ed.base`, so closing the tab drops the document with no question and no Reopen Closed Tab entry. (b) openInto reuses it as an empty tab. onConnected (1443-1445) then calls `ed.setValue(state)` for each pending entry without checking whether the tab has a picture of its own by now. (c) When connected, a failed load in openDocument still resolves as opened, and the empty tab keeps `docFile`. Opening the file again only activates that tab, and a picture later loaded into it is saved over the .scumble without a question (saveDocument's in-place stat sees the file unchanged).
scenario: Offline start (API-only user, ComfyUI not running) with a session tab whose base is not in the mirror. The tab shows 'will be restored once ComfyUI is connected'. The user drops a PNG into it and edits it for ten minutes, then starts ComfyUI: the old state replaces the picture, its layers and its history. Or, while connected, a .scumble whose picture fails to decode in this session (a huge document without the worker pool, a decoder failure) opens as an empty tab named after the file. Loading another image into it and pressing Ctrl+S overwrites the .scumble.
fix: In openDocument, when ed.base is still null after restore(), clear ed.docFile on that tab and throw ("could not be opened: <status>"), so openDocumentFromUi reports it and the tab is not bound to the file. Optionally make closeDocument and rememberClosed treat a tab with a _rawStates entry as holding a document: ask on close, and keep the raw state on the closed list. No onConnected change is needed: setValue's lastValueString early return already protects a tab that has loaded a picture of its own.
why: Only partly holds; the headline scenario (b) is refuted. In restore(), the failed setValue has already set lastValueString = raw (inpaint_canvas.js:24763) before the load failed. After the user loads a PNG into the parked tab, onConnected's setValue(state) gets the same string with this.base set, so it returns at once (24762). The PNG and its edits stay, and the raw state is dropped (1446). (a) holds: closing a parked tab asks nothing (closeDocument tests editor.base) and leaves no closed entry (rememberClosed returns on !ed.base). The state survives in autosave.1.json, though, which Settings › Local files › Earlier states opens, and parking only happens offline for a base that is not in the mirror. (c) holds but is rare. setValue catches its own errors and sets a red 'Could not restore canvas' line, so openDocument resolves as opened with an empty tab that keeps docFile, and opening the same file again only activates that tab. If the user loads another picture into it (openInto reuses it, since !ed.base) and presses Ctrl+S, saveDocument overwrites the .scumble in place without a question. It needs a decode failure while connected, followed by two user actions after a red error.

claim: handleUpload and handleRawUpload write mirror files in place with fsp.writeFile, which truncates and then writes (files.js:89, 121). They also pick a free name with existsSync before an await (87-89). (a) An upload whose hash name already exists truncates and rewrites a complete file that other states still name. This happens to every layer after an undo or redo of a canvas or turn step, which marks all layers dirty (inpaint_canvas.js:14606, 14665), and after a stroke followed by its undo. (b) Two overwrite:false uploads of the same name in flight both get the same free name. The second then sees the file the first has just created and skips its own write.
scenario: (a) Two tabs share mirror files: a document and a Save As copy of it are both open, and the open reused the files with the same bytes (docfile.js:721). In one tab the user crops and undoes, so its layers re-upload under the names the other tab's autosave and generation 1 hold. If Scumble is killed during the rewrite of a 15k layer (Task Manager, an update restart, a crash; the rewrite is hundreds of MB and takes a second or more), that file is cut short. The other tab's layer comes back broken at the next start. A .scumble save reading the file at that moment fails with '... changed while it was saved'. (b) Two pastes, both named image.png, upload at once in two tabs. Both get the same free name, the second tab's ref names the first tab's bytes, and its base is the other picture after a restore or in a run.
fix: For an overwrite:true upload under a hash name, skip the write when the file already exists with the same size. Otherwise write to <name>.uploading-<seq> and rename it into place. For free names, reserve the name atomically with fsp.open(path, 'wx') in a loop that moves to the next name on EEXIST.
why: The code shows both parts. (a) handleUpload and handleRawUpload rewrite an existing hash-named file in place with fsp.writeFile, which truncates and then writes (files.js:89, 121). An undo or redo of a canvas or turn step marks every layer dirty (inpaint_canvas.js:14606, 14665), so this happens to every layer. (b) freeName checks existsSync before the await on arrayBuffer, so two concurrent overwrite:false uploads of the same name can get the same name, and the second then skips its write or races it. Both windows are narrow. (a) needs the main process to die during a sub-second rewrite of identical bytes, for example a native crash or a quit that runs past the 120 s flush timeout. (b) needs two same-named uploads in flight at once. The damage is real, but the chance is small, so the severity is lowered to nice.

claim: 'Save to recipe' overwrites the held recipe with whatever graph the ComfyUI page's active workflow tab shows. Nothing checks that this is the graph the window loaded: canSave is phase === 'page' && !!recipe, and recipeLoaded is ignored. ComfyUI's frontend opens a recipe through loadApiJson/loadGraphData as a new workflow tab and keeps the user's other tabs (they persist in persist:comfyui), so the active tab is often a different graph.
scenario: The window holds recipe B, and the user's own workflow and recipe A are still open as ComfyUI tabs. The user clicks one of those tabs and edits it, then clicks Scumble's 'Save to recipe'. Or loadRecipe failed: recipeNote says 'The graph did not load', but the button stays enabled. save() (comfyview.js:495-517) reads graphToPrompt() of the active tab and calls saveComfyGraph with heldId B (main.js:1027). recipes.save overwrites B's user file with an unrelated graph, and a shipped B gets a user copy that stands in for it. A held Comfy Cloud recipe takes any graph without the Inpaint Canvas node through fromCloudGraph. There is no undo.
fix: Keep canSave false while recipeLoaded is false (offer only Save as new then). When loadRecipe succeeds, record the active workflow's name or path (app.workflowManager / the tab name passed to loadGraphData/loadApiJson). Have save() with !asNew read it again in READ_JS, and refuse or ask when it differs: 'The page shows another graph than <recipe>: save it as a new recipe, or switch back to its tab'.
why: The code shows no check. state() sets canSave = phase === 'page' && !!recipe and ignores recipeLoaded (comfyview.js:571-574). save() (495-517) reads graphToPrompt() of whatever workflow the page shows and passes heldId. saveComfyGraph (main.js) only checks that the InpaintCanvas node is present for a held ComfyUI recipe, or absent for a held Comfy Cloud recipe. So a different tab of the same kind passes, and so does a page that kept its own graph after a failed or skipped load ('The graph did not load', stayed()). Severity is lower than the claim: the user has to switch tabs or press Save after a failed load. 'Often' is overstated, because after Edit in ComfyUI the active tab is the loaded one. A shipped recipe that gets overwritten comes back by removing the copy. Only a user's own recipe is lost for good.

claim: When finish() falls back to copying the temp file over the target in place (the target is hard-linked, or a busy rename), a failure during that copy goes through step() -> drop(). drop() deletes the temp, which is the only complete copy of the new bytes, after the copy has already truncated or removed the old target.
scenario: An export of 1.2 GB goes over an existing 200 MB file that a viewer holds open (the rename fails EBUSY) or that has a second hard link. The start check needs only size + 1 MB, which the temp then uses up, so the in-place copy runs out of space halfway. libuv's copyfile unlinks the destination on failure on Linux; on Windows CopyFileW leaves it overwritten and partial. drop() (filesaves.js:170-177) then removes the fsynced temp. Both the old export and the new one are gone.
fix: Once the in-place copy has started, do not delete the temp on failure. Mark the save dead and remove it from the map by hand, keep the temp registered, and put its path in the error ('the new file is kept at <temp>'). Optionally, in start(), when inPlace is true or the rename may fall back, require free >= 2 * size - oldSize.
why: Confirmed. A copyFile failure in finish() (filesaves.js:119-124) throws inside step(), so drop() (170-177) calls removeTemp and deletes the fsynced temp, the only complete copy. On Windows CopyFileW has by then partly overwritten the target; libuv on Linux unlinks the destination on error. It needs a rare combination: the in-place path (the target has a second hard link, or another program holds it open with write sharing but not delete sharing, so the rename fails while CopyFileW can still write), and a failure partway. The extra space the in-place copy needs (size minus the old size) is not checked by start(), which checks only size + 1 MB. An I/O error would also do it.

claim: When upscale on an API model reaches its own timeout, it rejects through a Promise.race without stopping the run. key_screen cancels the run when its own race times out (host.cancelRuns), and realism_pass passes a deadline; upscale does neither.
scenario: upscale {scope: 'document', timeout: 300} on Magnific: at 300 s the agent gets 'the upscale timed out', while the provider job keeps running and is charged. Later it replaces the base, scaling every layer, or adds a result layer, with nobody waiting for it.
fix: In the timeout branch, call host.cancelRuns(ed) before rejecting, as key_screen does, and add the cancel's `said` to the error. Alternatively, pass a deadline into host.runUpscale.
why: Confirmed. The API branch of upscale races host.runUpscale against a timer that only rejects (renderer/commands.js:1667-1671). It never calls host.cancelRuns, as key_screen does (:1742), so the run lands later (a new base or a result layer) after the agent was told it timed out. A provider usually charges a submitted job whether or not it is cancelled, so the money claim is weak. The real harm is the late, unannounced change to the document. The default limit is 1800 s, so this mostly happens with an explicit short timeout.

claim: mapExtras makes relight's lights follow a turn, flip or straighten, but the built-in Gradient fill layer's angle and Centre X / Y (inpaint_filters.js 1294-1305) are canvas-relative and never mapped. The status line says every layer turned with the picture, yet the gradient's direction relative to the content changes.
scenario: A Gradient fill layer darkening the top of a landscape (linear, angle 90). Image › Rotate canvas 90° clockwise: the base, every layer and the gradient layer's mask turn, but the gradient still darkens the canvas top, which is now the scene's left side. Flip horizontal leaves an angled or off-centre gradient unmirrored. A radial gradient with its centre at 30 % / 50 % stays there after the turn, though its subject moved to 50 % / 30 %.
fix: In mapExtras, for filter === "gradient": add the quarter turns to angle and mirror it for a flip, map Centre X / Y through A as fractions of the old size into the new, and add a straighten's degrees. The canvas step already holds the old params, so undo puts them back.
why: Confirmed. mapExtras (5436-5494) maps the history, saved selections, maps, relight's lights (and aims), boxes and the export size. The Gradient fill's angle and Centre X / Y (inpaint_filters.js 1294-1305) are relative to the canvas: fillPixels draws over the full size and origin. Nothing maps them on a turn, a flip or a straighten. turnDocumentNow turns the gradient layer's mask but not its direction, while the status line says every layer turned. Severity lowered: the layer stays parametric, nothing is lost, and the wrong direction shows at once and is fixed with one slider (the angle plus or minus 90, or mirrored).

claim: selectLogits' main-thread loop (canvas backend, or tiles with the pool off) inverts for intersect first and then applies the layer clip only where a > 0. With jobInvert, the complement is therefore not subtracted where the layer is transparent. The worker fixed exactly this: its comment at inpaint_worker.js ~1338 notes that otherwise "Shift+Alt keeps the layer's transparent pixels". The window copy did not get the fix.
scenario: Canvas backend (Settings › Rendering › Tile engine off). A selection over a region, Object source = active layer on a cut-out layer, Shift+Alt+click the object (intersect). Every previously selected pixel where the layer is transparent stays selected, instead of only the object's pixels inside the old selection.
fix: Compute inside = v > 0 && !(clip && !clip[y*W+x]), then a = inside ? (jobInvert ? 0 : 255) : (jobInvert ? 255 : 0), as the worker does.
why: Confirmed. The main-thread loop at 8055-8056 sets a = v > 0 ? (inv ? 0 : 255) : (inv ? 255 : 0), and only then applies the clip, and only where a > 0. With intersect (jobInvert, bandMode subtract), a pixel where the layer is transparent and v <= 0 gets a = 0, so it is not subtracted and stays selected. The worker computes inside = v > 0 && clip first (inpaint_worker.js 1348-1351), and its comment names exactly this bug. The window copy never got the fix. It only affects the canvas backend or tiles with the pool off, Object source active layer, and Shift+Alt.

claim: Two held-key states are cleared only by their own keyup: Space-pan (spaceDown) and the \ peek (peekHold / peekBase, in the _docKeyUp at ~3163). Nothing resets them on window blur or visibility change, so releasing the key outside the window leaves the state stuck on.
scenario: Hold Space to pan, Alt+Tab to another app (or a notification takes focus), release Space there. Back in Scumble, every left click pans and no brush paints until Space is tapped again. Holding \ to peek at the base and losing focus the same way leaves every layer hidden on screen until \ is pressed again, which looks as if the layers vanished.
fix: On window blur and document visibilitychange (hidden): clear spaceDown, peekHold, peekBase and peekCode, reset the ipc-pan and peek-button classes, remove the pending Space keyup listener, and redraw.
why: Confirmed. spaceDown is cleared only by a keyup listener added at 3820-3830. peekHold and peekBase are cleared only in _docKeyUp (3175) and on close (3227). There is no blur or visibilitychange handler in the editor or the shell. A key released outside the window leaves Space-pan on: every left click pans (6168), and brush rings and overlays are suppressed. A \ released outside the window leaves the base-only view on. One tap of Space or \ recovers it: the existing keyup listener fires, and the \ press is ignored while peekBase is set, but its keyup clears the state.

claim: `computeDepthMap` and `depthFromLayer` take `geometryToken()` at the start, build the map with `xf = [W,0,0,H,0,0]` from the old size, and rely on `setMap`'s token check to drop a map whose geometry moved. `geometrySeq` only increases in `followGeometry`, the turn and the straighten. `restoreGeometry` (used by undo/redo of `canvas` / `turn` steps at 14598 / 14659 and by snapshot restores) never increases it. `depthPending` is also not in `turnBlocked()`, so such an undo is allowed during a depth run.
scenario: Extend the canvas by 1000 px on the left and add a relight layer (this starts `ensureDepthMap()` in the background; with Detail fine/finest it runs many seconds). Before it lands, Ctrl+Z twice to take back the relight layer and the extend. The depth map then lands with an xf for the extended size: shifted by 1000 px and larger than the document. Relight shadows, depth limits and lens blur use the wrong depth, and the map is saved in the .scumble file.
fix: Increase `geometrySeq` in `restoreGeometry`, or in `applySnapshot` for canvas/turn steps whose xf or size differ. Optionally add `depthPending` to `turnBlocked()`.
why: The mechanism is confirmed. `geometrySeq` increases only in `followGeometry` (5547) and the turn and straighten paths (5378, 5732). `restoreGeometry` (5525-5535) and the canvas/turn branches of `applySnapshot` never increase it. `computeDepthMap` takes its token at 13068 and builds `xf = [W,0,0,H,0,0]` from the size at its start (13176). `turnBlocked()` (5303-5313) does not include `depthPending`, so undoing an extend during a depth run is allowed, and the map lands with the extended size's xf. Severity lowered: the window is a running depth job, and the depth row's fingerprint stale check (`mapStale`, 13864) will probably mark such a map as stale, so the user gets a 'recompute' hint. The map is still wrong and is saved.

claim: `editDepth` reads `this.maps.depth` before two awaits (`selectionCanvasSettled`, then `setMap`'s upload) and derives the new map from that copy. Two edits that overlap (two quick clicks of Flatten/Smooth, or a plugin calling it twice) both start from the same map. The second `setMap` overwrites the first edit's result while the undo list shows both steps.
scenario: Select an area and click Smooth twice quickly at 15k, where `selectionCanvasSettled` waits for chains. The visible map holds only one smoothing pass; Ctrl+Z goes to a state with one pass, and the history lists two.
fix: Serialise depth edits through a promise chain, or re-read `this.maps.depth` after the awaits and refuse when it changed. Pass `geometryToken()` to `setMap`.
why: Confirmed. `editDepth` (13715-13766) reads `const map = this.maps.depth` before `await this.selectionCanvasSettled(...)` and derives `nextMap` from that copy. `setMap` (13585-13640) records `prev` as the map current at its own time. So two overlapping Smooth or Flatten clicks both derive from the same map: the second `setMap` replaces the first's result, and two undo steps are listed. Also no geometry token is passed, so a recompute or turn landing during the await is overwritten by a map derived from the old one. This needs two clicks inside the await window, so nice.

claim: A new result is named 'Result ' + (history.length + 1). After Clear history (which keeps the layers), or after a restore that trimmed the history to its last 100 entries, the numbers start again and repeat names of layers that still exist. findLayer resolves an exact name to the first, lowest match.
scenario: Results 1 to 5 exist as layers. Clear history, then Generate: the new layer is also called 'Result 1'. An agent reads 'Result 1 added' and calls set_layer / remove_layer with layer 'Result 1': it changes or deletes the old layer, not the new one. The panel shows two rows with the same name.
fix: Number new results from a per-document counter saved in the state, or from max(existing 'Result N') + 1.
why: Confirmed. A new result is named 'Result ' + (this.history.length + 1) (18965-18966). clearHistory (21376-21386) empties the history and keeps the layers, and getValue keeps only history.slice(-100) (24711), so names repeat. commands.js findLayer (157-172) resolves an exact name to the first match, the lowest layer. Agents mostly address layers by id, and the clash needs Clear history or more than 100 results, so the impact is small.

claim: If the stitch worker fails during 'finish', the selection window mask is lost: its buffer went to the worker and an ok:false reply does not send it back. The window fallback then re-reads the document's current selection (`selectionWindow(editor)`), which may be minutes after the click, and stitches the answer with that mask at the old bbox.
scenario: The user generates on area A with a 60 s API run. While waiting, the user selects area B to prepare the next run. The stitch worker's finish throws (an OffscreenCanvas or getImageData allocation failure for a large patch, a worker crash). The window fallback succeeds and lands the result with B's mask clipped to A's box: the edit is cut away where B does not cover A, and pasted where B overlaps the box but A was not selected.
fix: In the error reply of the worker's 'finish' job, send msg.sel back with its buffer transferred (wrap stitchJob's finish in a try that returns sel on failure), and restore sel.data from it in finishResultAsync's catch. If the mask is still gone, refuse the landing ('the stitch failed') rather than reading the current selection.
why: Confirmed. finishResultAsync sends sel.data.buffer to the stitch worker as a transfer (stitch.js:957). The worker's error reply (stitch_worker.js catch) sends nothing back, so the window's copy is detached. The fallback then reads `area ? windowMask(area.window()) : selectionWindow(editor)` (961). A plain Generate passes no area (runProvider's area is opts.area || null), so the fallback reads the selection as it is now. The comment says so outright ('the selection's window as it is now'). If the user has changed the selection since the click, the answer is cut with the new mask at the run's bbox. If the selection was cleared, selectionWindowPixels calls editor.sel.readRect on null and the paid answer does not land at all. The trigger, the worker failing while the window path would succeed, is rare.

claim: queueGenerate reads the server's text-encoder files for the prompt upsampler's file check as CLIPLoader.input.required.clip_name[0]. That only works for the older [[names], {...}] combo form. With the newer ['COMBO', { options }] form, which loras.js comboOf, comfy.js probe (165) and comfycloud.js choicesOf all handle, upClips is the string 'COMBO'. files is then null, and wireUpsampler skips the 'file not on your ComfyUI' fallback without a word. This is a second copy of the combo-parsing rule that has drifted from the others.
scenario: flux3_klein_local ships its Prompt upsampler row switched on (up_switch.switch true). Take a user without the 6.7 GB qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler file, on a ComfyUI that serves CLIPLoader in the COMBO form. Instead of 'The prompt went as typed: the prompt upsampler's file ... is not on your ComfyUI', the graph is queued with up_clip naming the missing file, and ComfyUI refuses the whole prompt at validation ('Value not in list'). Every Klein run fails until the user finds the row and switches it off.
fix: Replace the hand-read with comboOf(this.objectInfo, "CLIPLoader", "clip_name") and pass its result (or null) as files, so there is one combo rule for both forms.
why: The code shows the drift. host.js:5585-5586 reads CLIPLoader.input.required.clip_name[0] and accepts it only when it is an array, which is the older form alone. The project's own rule (loras.js comboOf 62-78, 'never spec[0] alone'; comfy.js 165; comfycloud.js choicesOf) handles both forms, and comboOf is already imported into host.js (line 56). With files null, wireUpsampler (comfyprompt.js:361) silently skips the 'file not on your ComfyUI' fallback. The claimed failure is latent, not current: the snapshot's object_info fixture (tools/refs/comfy_templates/object_info.json) serves CLIPLoader.clip_name in the older [[names]] form, and only V3 nodes (17 inputs there, e.g. TextEncodeMOSSImageEdit) use ['COMBO', {options}]. The scenario needs ComfyUI to move CLIPLoader to the V3 schema. Even then the result is a visible validation refusal from ComfyUI, not wrong pixels or money. So it is a cheap hardening of a drifted copy, at nice.

claim: Both shadow marches (Rust and twin) take the first `taps` points of a fixed 16-point Vogel spiral (`VOGEL_16[t]`; kernels_js.js:1591-1601 `relightVogel` builds N = 16 and then slices). They do not build an n-point disc as `vogelDisc(n)` in inpaint_lensblur.js does. The 4 taps of a full march therefore all sit within 0.47 of the light's radius. The single tap of the quick march sits off-centre, at (+0.177 r, 0).
scenario: Point light, Diffusion 100, on a 4096 x 2731 depth map: radius = 0.05 x long side. During a drag the quick march (inpaint_canvas.js ~23705: taps = quick ? 1 : 4) runs on the quarter map, where r = 51 px, and casts shadows from a light 9 px (36 map px) to the right of the handle. When the full march lands, the shadows jump back. The full map's penumbra is about half the width the Diffusion value asks for (tap radii 0.18-0.47 r, sqrt((i + 0.5)/16)). The two twins agree byte for byte, so px_test cannot see this. PLAN_RELIGHT_BUILD.md §4.3 asks for 'a Vogel disc of radius', and the 'first n of 16' table does not give one.
fix: Low-risk part: for taps == 1, march from the light's own position (tap (0, 0)) in both relight.rs and relightVogel. This changes only the quick drag preview and no exported bytes. Rebuild the wasm, then run px_test and the relight gate. Changing the 4-tap set to a full 4-point disc, sqrt((i+0.5)/4), is a look change. Say the effect to the user first and let them judge, as the working rules ask, before touching it.
why: The mechanism is as described. VOGEL_16 (relight.rs:5-22) has radii sqrt((i+0.5)/16), and relightVogel (kernels_js.js:1591-1601) builds 16 points and slices off the first n. The caller (inpaint_canvas.js:23701) passes 1 tap for quick maps and 4 for full ones. The quick march's only tap therefore sits at (+0.177 r, 0), not on the light. The 4 full taps lie within 0.18-0.47 r, centroid about (0.07, 0.05) r. Point and spot lights go through the f64 twin (kernels.js:477-479), and it has the same table. Two parts of the claim are overstated, though. PLAN_RELIGHT_BUILD.md line 404 explicitly says 'the Vogel disc as a const table of 16 taps, `taps` picks the first n', so the prefix is what the plan chose, even though §4.3 line 200 names vogelDisc. And 'half the penumbra the Diffusion value asks for' is a calibration matter: the 0.05 x long-side constant is arbitrary, and the user judged the look by eye before 0.1.47. What remains is the off-centre single tap. During a drag the quick shadows sit about 0.18 r to the right, which is about 0.27 % of the long side at the default Diffusion of 30 and 0.9 % at 100. At landing they shift back by about 0.11 r, on top of the hard-to-soft change that landing brings anyway. Quick maps never reach an export (relightIdle waits for the full march), so no saved pixels are wrong.

claim: lutFromCube rescales the table's output values by DOMAIN_MIN / DOMAIN_MAX. In the .cube format the domain is the input range the lattice spans; output values are not normalised by it. Neither applyLut nor the 3D-texture shader maps the pixel into the domain: both index the lattice over 0..1.
scenario: Load a valid .cube with DOMAIN_MIN 0 0 0 / DOMAIN_MAX 2 2 2 (a scene-linear or HDR export). Every output is halved, so the picture comes out about half as bright. A pixel value of 1.0 also reads the lattice's last point instead of its middle. With DOMAIN_MIN -0.1 every output is shifted up instead. Files with the default 0..1 domain are unaffected. The wrong values are also baked into the uploaded lutToCanvas PNG, so they survive a save.
fix: Keep the parsed outputs, clamped to 0..1. When the domain is not 0..1, resample the lattice once at parse time onto a 0..1 input grid: trilinear interpolation in the original lattice, inputs outside the domain clamped. Then applyLut, the 3D texture and lutToCanvas / lutFromImage stay as they are. Add a lutFromCube unit case with DOMAIN_MAX 2 2 2 and an identity table, which must map 0.5 to 0.5.
why: The code shows it. lutFromCube (inpaint_filters.js:394-398) rescales each output value by `(v - domainMin) / (domainMax - domainMin)` and clamps it. In the .cube format DOMAIN_MIN / DOMAIN_MAX give the input range the lattice spans; the table's outputs are not normalised by it. Both lookups index the lattice over 0..1 input with no domain mapping: applyLut uses `px * (N-1)/255` (:438-458), and the GL path samples at `(c*(N-1)+0.5)/N` (inpaint_filters_gl.js:113). So a DOMAIN 0..2 file comes out at half brightness and reads the wrong lattice cell. The wrong values are also baked into the lutToCanvas PNG. Nothing in docs, tests or plugins handles DOMAIN differently, and it is not a known issue. The severity goes down to nice: only .cube files with a non-default DOMAIN are affected, which creative, display-referred LUTs rarely carry. The defect shows up at once on screen and costs no data.

claim: applyHaze, the CPU twin, samples the depth map at pass pixel corners (`origin[1] + y`, `origin[0] + x` at :171 / :175). Its shader samples at pixel centres (`pictureUv(uv) * u_pictureSize` = origin + x + 0.5), and the dehaze and relight CPU twins add 0.5 as well.
scenario: Without WebGL2, or after the haze program has failed, view a 15k picture fitted to the window (pass scale about 0.1, depth map 4096 wide). passToMap's m[0] is about 2.7, so the CPU haze reads the map about 1.4 map pixels up-left of where the GPU haze reads it. With Edges snap on, the haze boundary along a depth edge then lands about 5 image pixels away from where the GPU path and the export put it.
fix: Use `origin[1] + y + 0.5` and `origin[0] + x + 0.5` in applyHaze, as applyDehaze and applyRelight do. Optionally add a GL-vs-CPU haze parity case at a preview scale (around 0.1) to the depthfx gate.
why: The code shows it. The haze CPU twin computes `py = origin[1] + y` and `px_x = origin[0] + x` (inpaint_depthfx.js:171, :175). The shader uses `pictureUv(uv) * u_pictureSize` = u_pictureOrigin + gl_FragCoord.xy (inpaint_filters_gl.js:1005, :1010), which is origin + x + 0.5. The dehaze twin (inpaint_depthfx.js:334, :338) and the relight twin (inpaint_relight.js:1609, :1613) both add 0.5 and call the same snapField, so haze is the odd one out. The impact is small: the CPU twin runs only without WebGL2, above g.max, or after the haze program failed. At scale 1 the offset is a fraction of a map pixel; only at a zoomed-out preview scale does it grow to about a map pixel. nice is right.

claim: Every import into the mirror goes through `${dest}.importing-${process.pid}`, so two opens of documents that carry the same file, or that compute the same free name, share one temp. The locks are per .scumble path, and the window can run two opens at once. Main maps any ENOENT during an open to 'is not there any more' and removes the file from Open Recent (main.js:1134).
scenario: Two .scumble files are Save As variants of one picture, so both carry files/input/inpaint_canvas/n1_base_<hash>.png. On a PC whose mirror lacks that file (another PC, or after Clean up), the user selects both in Explorer and presses Enter. Each second start sends documents:pending, and openPendingDocuments runs twice at once (shell.js:3012-3015). Both copyEntry calls open the same temp with 'w'. The first renames it over dest; the second's rename then fails with ENOENT. So the second open reports 'B.scumble is not there any more (moved or deleted); it left Open Recent' although the file exists, and drops it from the menu. In the other order, the second open truncates the temp just before the first renames it, and the first tab loads a layer file that is still being rewritten.
fix: Make the temp name unique per call (`.importing-${pid}-${++seq}`), serialise imports per destination key in Documents (a Map of promises), and in main.js treat ENOENT as 'not there any more' only when fs.existsSync(req.path) is false.
why: Confirmed in the code. copyEntry uses `${dest}.importing-${process.pid}` (docfile.js:632-633), and Documents.run locks per .scumble path only, so two opens of different files run at once. openPendingDocuments can run twice concurrently (shell.js:3012-3015), once per documents:pending from a second start. If both documents carry a file the mirror lacks, both stat calls miss and both copyEntry calls open the same temp with 'w'. libuv opens with FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so the first rename succeeds and the second rename fails with ENOENT. main.js:1134 maps that to 'not there any more' and drops the file from Open Recent. The first tab may also read the file while the second still writes it. The trigger is narrow: several documents that share files, opened together on a PC whose mirror lacks those files. A retry works because the file is then reused.

claim: writeDocument does not check for a read-only target before it writes, although FileSaves.start does (filesaves.js:59). The rename then fails with EPERM, renameRetry retries it for 2 s, and the save reports it as 'in use by another program'.
scenario: Ctrl+S on a .scumble with the read-only attribute set (copied from an archive or a stick, or set by a sync tool). The whole file, gigabytes at 15k, is written to the temp first. The save then fails with the wrong reason, and the user goes looking for a program that holds the file.
fix: Stat the target before writing, as FileSaves.start does, and fail at once with '<name> is read-only' when (mode & 0o200) is 0.
why: Confirmed. writeDocument (docfile.js:420-505) writes the whole temp before renameRetry, and FileSaves.start's read-only check (filesaves.js:59) has no counterpart in documents.write or writeDocument. On Windows a rename over a read-only target fails with EPERM. renameRetry retries it for about 2 s (20 x 100 ms), BUSY includes EPERM, and the message becomes 'in use by another program'. Only time and a misleading message are lost: the temp is removed and the target is untouched.

claim: sweepTemps writes the temp list empty after trying each delete, even when a delete failed for a reason other than ENOENT. The catch says 'gone already' for every error. The will-quit sweep does the same.
scenario: A 3 GB export to a USB drive is cut off because the app was killed. At the next start the drive is not plugged in (or an antivirus holds the temp), unlinkSync fails, and the list is written empty. photo.png.saving-1234-5 then stays on the drive for good, and later starts never retry.
fix: Keep a path in the list when its unlink fails with anything other than ENOENT, and also when its folder is not reachable (fs.existsSync(path.dirname(p)) is false), so a temp on a missing drive is retried at a later start.
why: Confirmed. sweepTemps (docfile.js:381-389) empties the registry after trying each unlink, whatever the error, and the catch comment says 'gone already'. A temp whose delete failed is then never retried. One correction: a drive that is not plugged in returns ENOENT (path not found) on Windows, so the proposed 'keep non-ENOENT failures' rule would not cover the finding's own USB scenario. Only an EBUSY or EPERM delete would be kept. The impact is a stray .saving-* file, which is litter, not data loss.

claim: AgentBackend.ensure() is not single-flight, and it calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock() as a probe. Two concurrent first calls each try the socket and the lock, and the owning process then runs startApp() twice. In a secondary process, a lock request that fails fires 'second-instance' in the primary, and the primary shows its hidden window.
scenario: (a) An MCP proxy whose instance quit gets two parallel tool calls. Both connects fail, both get the lock (a second request in the same process returns true), and both call startApp(). The second call rotates and sweeps again, adds a second will-quit and second-instance listener, then throws 'Failed to register protocol: scumble' at installProtocol, so that tool call fails with that message. (b) Two MCP clients start within about 1 s with no Scumble running. Process A holds the lock but is not listening yet (whenReady plus startApp). B's connect fails, and its requestSingleInstanceLock() fires A's second-instance -> onSecondInstance -> showWindow(). The agent's headless window pops up, headless becomes false, and maybeQuit no longer ends the instance when the agents leave (windowVisible).
fix: Single-flight ensure() (this.starting ??= this._ensure().finally(() => { this.starting = null; })). Check this.own again after each await inside the loop. Register second-instance only once (a module flag). Optionally have onSecondInstance ignore an argv that carries --mcp or --cmd, so a probing agent start does not show the window.
why: Case (a) holds in the code. ensure() checks this.own only once, at the top (main.js:1439). Two parallel tool calls on a proxy whose instance quit both fail LocalClient.connect. The first takes the lock and runs startApp. The second, inside its loop, calls requestSingleInstanceLock(), which returns true again in the same process (Electron's HasSingleInstanceLock short-circuit, inferred from its source). It then adds a second second-instance and will-quit listener, rotates and sweeps again, and throws at installProtocol's protocol.handle ('Failed to register protocol: scumble'), so that one tool call fails. Case (b) needs B's lock request to land in the gap between A's lock and A's local.listen. On a cold start A's connect error arrives only once the message loop runs, so that gap is about one tick (inferred). Very narrow. Small impact overall.

claim: readError cuts a non-JSON error body to 300 characters but returns a JSON body's error/detail as full JSON.stringify. fal, Replicate, WaveSpeed, BFL's submit, OpenAI, Gemini, ToAPIs and legacy Comfy Cloud put this text straight into the Error message. A validation error that echoes the input (FastAPI/pydantic-style detail entries with an "input" field) can then carry the whole base64 data URI of the crop or a reference. Inferred: whether fal's 422 echoes the input is not verified.
scenario: A fal edit with a crop that is too large for the route is refused with 422, detail [{loc:["body","image_url"], msg, input:"data:image/png;base64,...(8 MB)"}]. The Error message is about 8 MB. It goes to the status line, to an MCP agent's generate error (filling its context) and to the assistant; only the log record caps it (2000).
fix: In readError, cut the JSON-derived message too (for example to 500 characters), and before stringifying drop or shorten "input" fields in detail arrays.
why: The code part is confirmed. util.js:28-31 returns a JSON body's error, detail, message or status in full, with no cut on either the string or the JSON.stringify branch. Only the non-JSON branch is cut, to 300 characters (33). fal, Replicate, WaveSpeed, BFL's submit, OpenAI and Gemini put this text straight into the Error message. The assistant passes tool error text to the model uncapped (assistant/index.js errorResult 962-964), and the MCP path has no cap either. The trigger is a provider's 422 echoing the input. FastAPI/pydantic v2 validation errors do carry an "input" field, and fal's error format includes it, so an image-validation refusal of a data-URI field would echo megabytes. That trigger was not run here, and it needs an image-related validation error, which is rare.

claim: set_layer's geometry (x, y, w, h) checks no lock, own or group, although the editor forbids moving a locked layer and refuseLayer guards flip, centre, match_edges and transform. set_text rewrites and renders a locked text layer and only then throws for `angle` (line 2446), keeping the change without touch() or notifyChanged. The assistant's policy guards only `target.locked` (policy.js:527), while list_layers reports a group's lock as `locked_by_group`.
scenario: The user locks the group 'Background' that holds the layer 'Sky'. The assistant calls set_layer {layer: Sky, x: 200}: decide sees locked false, setLayer has no soft field, so the call is AUTO and the command moves the layer. An external agent's set_layer moves an own-locked layer as well. set_text {layer: <locked text>, text: 'x', angle: 5} changes the text, then answers with an error, so the agent believes nothing changed, and the list, thumbnail and autosave are not refreshed.
