fix: policy.decide: test target.locked || target.locked_by_group. set_text: check ed.isLocked(l) (or l.locked with angle) before any field is written. Optionally call refuseLayer in set_layer's geometry branch so external agents match the editor.
why: Partly confirmed. set_layer applies geometry with no lock check (renderer/commands.js:2029-2037). policy.js:525 says so on purpose ('the editor forbids it; the commands do not'), and decide() guards only target.locked (policy.js:527), while layerSummary reports a group lock as locked_by_group (commands.js:86). So the assistant moves a layer in a locked group without asking: setLayer (policy.js:456-463) returns AUTO for geometry alone. set_text writes the fields and renders the text layer first (commands.js:2437-2445), then throws for angle on a locked layer (:2446) without touch(). The change stays, the agent gets an error, and the lists and autosave are not refreshed. The failure is real, but the move is undoable and the external-agent side is documented design, so the severity is lowered to nice.

claim: The Bridge extends its 600 s timeout only by an explicit args.timeout, so an external MCP call that omits timeout is cut off at 600 s while the command keeps running under its own longer default: upscale waits 1800 s (commands.js:1644 and 1667), and generate / generate_new wait 600 s plus at least 30 s (commands.js:1902, 1923). docs/MCP.md:298 says 'a long generate always ends in the editor first', which holds only when timeout is passed. realism_pass (default 570) is the one command written for this rule; the assistant is safe because policy.clamp fills the defaults.
scenario: Claude Desktop calls upscale {scope: 'document'} on Topaz without timeout. At 600 s the agent gets 'command "upscale" did not answer in time', while the paid job keeps going and replaces the document minutes later. On the user's busy production ComfyUI, a generate waiting in the queue reports failure at 600 s and lands afterwards. A retry once the first run has landed queues or pays a second run.
fix: In the Bridge or mcp/server.js, when args.timeout is absent, take the command's declared params.timeout.default from describe() to compute `extra`, as policy.clamp does.
why: Confirmed in code. The Bridge extends BASE_TIMEOUT 600 s only by an explicit args.timeout (bridge.js:17, 90, 99). upscale defaults to 1800 s (commands.js:1632, 1644, 1667), and a provider generate has no own limit around ed.generate(). The assistant is covered by policy.clamp (TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS, policy.js:470). An external caller without timeout therefore gets 'did not answer in time' at 600 s while the command runs on. That contradicts docs/MCP.md:298. For generate on ComfyUI, the difference is only the tail after 600 s: both paths end in an error and the job goes on either way. Lowered to nice: the impact is a misleading early error, and money is spent only if the agent retries after the run lands (a retry during the run is refused by providerPending).

claim: set_node_params stores any value of at least 0 and saves it to settings.json for every tab and session. The Node params panel clamps the same fields to padding 0..4096, target_size 0..8192, feather 0..512 and multiple_of 1..256 (host.js:5746-5751), so the same rule exists twice and the command's copy has no upper bound.
scenario: An agent working on a 15000 x 10000 picture sends set_node_params {target_size: 20000}, meaning full resolution. External agents get no question, and the assistant's card shows only from and to. Every later local run asks the Inpaint Canvas node for a 20000 px crop, which exhausts VRAM on the user's production ComfyUI, and the app's own crop maths (stitch.js:434) takes it too. The panel then shows 20000, above its own maximum, until the user fixes it.
fix: Export the panel's fields table (key, min, max) from host.js. In set_node_params, clamp to it, or refuse with the allowed range.
why: The rule exists twice and has drifted. set_node_params stores Math.max(0, round(v)) with no upper bound and allows multiple_of 0 (renderer/commands.js:1466), and saves it to settings. The panel clamps to 0..4096 / 0..8192 / 0..512 / 1..256 (host.js:5746-5751, 5763). The scenario's consequence is wrong, though: the Inpaint Canvas node declares the same min/max on these INT inputs, and ComfyUI's prompt validation refuses a value above max ('bigger than max'), so the server's VRAM is not exhausted. The real effect is that every later local run is refused with a validation error, and the panel shows the out-of-range value until the user fixes it. stitch.js:433 guards multiple_of 0 on the app side. That makes it a small, persistent misconfiguration, not a should.

claim: generate clears ed.lastSentPrompt, lastRunNotes, lastLoras and lastPassError before its refusal 'a run is still going on this document' (line 1901). A refused second call therefore wipes the report fields of the run in flight.
scenario: Agent A's generate on fal is running. A second generate on the same document (another agent, or a retry after a Bridge timeout) clears the four fields and is refused. When A's run lands, A's answer reports prompt_sent null, notes [] and loras_sent []. Its failed() check has also lost lastPassError, so a failed Realism Pass box run waits out the timeout instead of failing at once.
fix: Move the providerPending refusal above the four resets, next to the wired check.
why: Confirmed. generate resets ed.lastSentPrompt, lastRunNotes, lastLoras and lastPassError (renderer/commands.js:1893-1896) before its providerPending refusal (:1901). A second generate on a document with a run in flight, from another external agent (the assistant's policy refuses busy documents first), wipes the in-flight run's report fields. The first call then answers prompt_sent null and notes [] (:1924). Narrow and cosmetic, apart from failed() missing a lastPassError that was set before the reset.

claim: `depthProxy` / `depthProxy1024Data` cache into `_depthProxies` keyed by `maxSize:dataVersion` and never evict; only `dropCompositeCaches` (turns, flips, canvas undo) clears the map. Every depth edit (`editDepth`) and recompute makes a new `dataVersion`. `mapHistogram` bounds its cache to 8 entries for the same reason ('a few versions, not every recompute'), so the two caches follow different rules. `similarityHistogram`'s `_simHistCache` likewise gains an entry for every `compositeVersion`.
scenario: At 15k the depth map is 4096 x 2731. With the depth view on (mapView 'depth', 23945) or a depth range preview, each Flatten / Offset / Smooth or Recompute adds a 2048 x 1365 canvas (11 MB) and a 2.8 MB Float32 array that stay referenced. Thirty depth edits keep about 400 MB alive.
fix: Keep only the current `dataVersion`'s proxies (clear the map when a key's version differs), or cap it as `_mapHistCache` is.
why: Confirmed. `depthProxy` (15892-15929) and `depthProxy1024Data` (15939-15966) add an entry keyed by `maxSize:dataVersion` and never evict it. Only `dropCompositeCaches` (5578) clears the map. `mapHistogram` caps its cache at 8 entries (15800). With the depth view on (23943-23953), every depth edit or recompute adds a 2048-px canvas (about 11 MB for a 4096 x 2731 map). `_simHistCache` also grows per compositeVersion, but its entries are 2 KB arrays, which is negligible. The growth is bounded by user actions, so it stays nice.

claim: The mirror's name rule in files.js (SAFE_NAME only) has drifted from the copy in docfile.js, which also refuses Windows device names and a trailing dot or space (docfile.js:186-192). docfile's comment calls its copy 'the mirror's own rule'.
scenario: The user opens a picture named aux.png (or con.jpg, nul.png, com1.png). loadFile keeps the stem, and files.js accepts and writes the name. Every Ctrl+S on that document then fails in documents.write with 'bad file name: aux.png' (docfile.mirrorPath, documents.js:186), so the document can never be saved as a .scumble. On Windows versions that still map such names to devices, the mirror write goes to the device and the base is gone after a restart.
fix: Export badPart from docfile.js and use it in files.js mirrorPath. In the upload handlers, map a refused name to a safe one (for example append '_' to the stem) instead of storing it.
why: Confirmed drift. files.js:12/24 accepts any SAFE_NAME, while docfile.js:186-192 also refuses Windows device names (con, prn, aux, nul, com1-9, lpt1-9, with any extension) and a trailing dot or space, and calls its copy 'the mirror's own rule'. loadFile's stem sanitiser (inpaint_canvas.js:18533) keeps 'aux' and appends the extension, so a picture named aux.png or con.jpg lands in the mirror. documents.write then throws 'bad file name: aux.png' from docfile.mirrorPath (documents.js:186), and that document can never be saved as a .scumble. This is rare, but the outcome is a hard failure.
